s.t: Buck was a big dog, and he lived on a farm in the Santa Clara Valley.
s.fr: Buck était un grand chien qui vivait dans une ferme de la vallée de Santa Clara.

s.t: Judge Miller owned the farm, and Buck was the king of it.
s.fr: La ferme appartenait au juge Miller, et Buck en était le roi.

s.t: All the other dogs on the farm obeyed Buck, and he loved the Judge and his family.
s.fr: Tous les autres chiens de la ferme obéissaient à Buck, et lui aimait le juge et sa famille.

s.t: Buck did not know that men in the north had found gold.
s.fr: Buck ignorait que, dans le Nord, des hommes avaient trouvé de l’or.

s.t: Those men wanted big strong dogs to pull their sleds in the snow.
s.fr: Ces hommes voulaient des chiens grands et forts pour tirer leurs traîneaux dans la neige.

s.t: Buck knew nothing about the cold, and he had never left the farm.
s.fr: Buck ne savait rien du froid, et il n’avait jamais quitté la ferme.

paras.summary: Buck, a big dog, rules the farm of Judge Miller in the Santa Clara Valley, and he does not know that men in the north want strong dogs for sleds.

s.t: Manuel worked on the farm, and he knew about the gold.
s.fr: Manuel, qui travaillait à la ferme, avait entendu parler de l’or.

s.t: Manuel liked to play games for money, and he always lost.
s.fr: Manuel aimait jouer de l’argent, et il perdait à chaque fois.

s.t: His wife and his children needed food, and he had no money to buy it.
s.fr: Sa femme et ses enfants manquaient de pain, et il n’avait pas de quoi en acheter.

s.t: "I will sell a dog," Manuel said to himself.
s.fr: « Je vais vendre un chien, » se dit Manuel.

s.t: "I will sell Buck, and then I will have money."
s.fr: « Je vendrai Buck, et alors j’aurai de l’argent. »

paras.summary: Manuel, a farm worker, loses money at games and decides to sell Buck to feed his family.

s.t: One night the Judge was away, and Manuel took Buck for a walk.
s.fr: Un soir que le juge était en voyage, Manuel emmena Buck se promener.

s.t: No one saw them go, and no one saw them come to the station.
s.fr: Personne ne les vit partir, et personne ne les vit arriver à la gare.

s.t: At the station a stranger waited, and he had money in his hand.
s.fr: À la gare attendait un inconnu, qui tenait de l’argent à la main.

s.t: "Is this the dog?" the stranger asked.
s.fr: « C’est le chien ? » demanda l’inconnu.

s.t: "This is the dog," Manuel said, "and he is a very big dog."
s.fr: « C’est bien lui, dit Manuel, et c’est une sacrée bête. »

s.t: "Is he a good dog?" the stranger asked.
s.fr: « C’est un bon chien ? » demanda l’inconnu.

s.t: "He is a very good dog," Manuel said.
s.fr: « Un très bon chien, » répondit Manuel.

paras.summary: While the Judge is away, Manuel takes Buck to a station, where a stranger waits with money.

s.t: "Give me the money," Manuel said.
s.fr: « Donnez-moi l’argent, » dit Manuel.

s.t: The stranger gave him the money, and Manuel gave him the dog.
s.fr: L’inconnu lui remit l’argent, et Manuel lui remit le chien.

s.t: Manuel put a rope around Buck's neck, and the stranger took the rope.
s.fr: Manuel passa une corde au cou de Buck, et l’inconnu prit la corde.

s.t: "You must go with this man, Buck," Manuel said.
s.fr: « Tu dois suivre ce monsieur, Buck, » dit Manuel.

s.t: Buck did not like the rope, and he did not like the stranger.
s.fr: Buck n’aimait pas cette corde, et il n’aimait pas davantage l’inconnu.

paras.summary: Manuel takes the money, gives Buck to the stranger with a rope around his neck, and tells him to be good.

s.t: Buck growled at the stranger, but the stranger did not stop.
s.fr: Buck gronda contre l’inconnu, mais celui-ci ne s’arrêta pas.

s.t: He pulled the rope, and Buck jumped at his throat.
s.fr: Il tira sur la corde, et Buck lui sauta à la gorge.

s.t: The stranger caught Buck by the neck and held the rope tight.
s.fr: L’inconnu attrapa Buck par le cou et serra la corde de toutes ses forces.

s.t: Buck could not breathe, and he fell down on the ground.
s.fr: Buck ne pouvait plus respirer, et il s’effondra sur le sol.

paras.summary: Buck growls and jumps at the stranger, who holds the rope tight until Buck falls down.

chapterList.title: The Man in the Red Sweater

s.t: Buck was in a box, and the box was in a train.
s.fr: Buck était enfermé dans une caisse, elle-même chargée à bord d’un train.

s.t: He had no food and no water, and he was very angry.
s.fr: Il n’avait ni à manger ni à boire, et il était fou de rage.

s.t: Each time a man came near the box, Buck growled at him.
s.fr: Chaque fois qu’un homme s’approchait de la caisse, Buck grondait contre lui.

s.t: The men laughed at Buck, and they hit the box with sticks.
s.fr: Les hommes se moquaient de Buck et frappaient la caisse à coups de bâton.

s.t: Buck was more and more angry, for no one had hit him before.
s.fr: La colère de Buck ne cessait de croître, car jamais personne ne l’avait frappé.

paras.summary: Buck is in a box on a train with no food or water, and he growls at the men who laugh at him and hit the box with sticks.

s.t: At last the train stopped in a big city.
s.fr: Enfin, le train s’arrêta dans une grande ville.

s.t: Four men put the box down on the ground, and a man came out.
s.fr: Quatre hommes déposèrent la caisse à terre, et un homme sortit.

s.t: The man wore a red sweater, and he had a club in his hand.
s.fr: L’homme portait un chandail rouge et tenait un gourdin à la main.

s.t: He opened the box, and Buck saw the light.
s.fr: Il ouvrit la caisse, et Buck revit le jour.

s.t: "Come out of the box, dog," the man said.
s.fr: « Sors de là, le chien, » dit l’homme.

s.t: Buck jumped at the man, but the man hit him with the club.
s.fr: Buck se jeta sur l’homme, mais celui-ci le frappa de son gourdin.

paras.summary: In a city the box is put down, and a man in a red sweater with a club opens it, and Buck jumps at him but is hit.

s.t: Buck fell down on the ground, and blood ran from his mouth.
s.fr: Buck tomba à terre, et le sang lui coula de la gueule.

s.t: Buck got up and jumped again, and again the man hit him.
s.fr: Buck se releva et bondit de nouveau, et de nouveau l’homme le frappa.

s.t: Again and again Buck jumped, and each time the club hit him.
s.fr: Buck bondit encore et encore, et chaque fois le gourdin s’abattit sur lui.

s.t: At last Buck could not get up.
s.fr: Enfin, Buck ne put plus se relever.

s.t: His body hurt, and he lay still for a long time.
s.fr: Tout son corps lui faisait mal, et il resta longtemps étendu sans bouger.

paras.summary: Each time Buck jumps, the man hits him with the club until Buck cannot get up.

s.t: "Do you want more?" the man asked.
s.fr: « Tu en veux encore ? » demanda l’homme.

s.t: Buck did not answer, and he did not jump again.
s.fr: Buck ne répondit pas, et il ne bondit plus.

s.t: "Now you know me," the man said, "and I know you."
s.fr: « Maintenant, tu me connais, dit l’homme, et moi, je te connais. »

s.t: "You will get food and water if you are good."
s.fr: « Tu auras à manger et à boire si tu es sage. »

s.t: The man gave him food and water, and Buck ate and drank.
s.fr: L’homme lui donna à manger et à boire, et Buck mangea et but.

s.t: Buck did not love the man, but he did what the man said.
s.fr: Buck n’aimait pas l’homme, mais il faisait ce que l’homme lui ordonnait.

paras.summary: The man says he will give Buck food and water if he is good, and Buck eats and drinks and does what the man says.

s.t: Buck learned that day that a man with a club was his master.
s.fr: Ce jour-là, Buck apprit qu’un homme armé d’un gourdin était son maître.

s.t: A dog must obey a master, and Buck did not forget it.
s.fr: Un chien doit obéir à son maître, et Buck ne l’oublia pas.

s.t: Other dogs came in boxes, and Buck saw the same men hit them with the same club.
s.fr: D’autres chiens arrivèrent dans des caisses, et Buck vit les mêmes hommes les frapper avec le même gourdin.

s.t: He saw that a dog could not fight a man with a club.
s.fr: Il comprit qu’un chien ne pouvait rien contre un homme armé d’un gourdin.

paras.summary: Buck learns that a man with a club is a master to be obeyed, and he sees other dogs beaten the same way.

chapterList.title: The Law of Club and Fang

s.t: The man in the red sweater sold Buck to two other men, and they took him north on a boat.
s.fr: L’homme au chandail rouge vendit Buck à deux autres hommes, qui l’emmenèrent vers le Nord en bateau.

s.t: The boat was big, and it went over the water for many days.
s.fr: Le bateau était grand, et la traversée dura de longs jours.

s.t: Buck and the other dogs sat in boxes, and the men gave them food and water.
s.fr: Buck et les autres chiens restaient dans leurs caisses, et les hommes leur donnaient à manger et à boire.

s.t: Some of the dogs were afraid, and some of them were angry.
s.fr: Certains chiens avaient peur, d’autres enrageaient.

s.t: Buck did not growl at the men, for he remembered the club.
s.fr: Buck ne grondait pas contre les hommes, car il se souvenait du gourdin.

paras.summary: Buck is sold to two men and taken north on a big boat, and he does not growl at them because he remembers the club.

s.t: At last the boat came to a cold place, and the men took Buck out of the box.
s.fr: Enfin le bateau atteignit une contrée froide, et les hommes sortirent Buck de sa caisse.

s.t: Buck put his feet on the ground, and the ground was white and wet.
s.fr: Buck posa les pattes sur le sol, qui était blanc et mouillé.

s.t: It was snow, but Buck did not know it.
s.fr: C’était de la neige, mais Buck ne le savait pas.

s.t: It was cold, and he had never seen snow before.
s.fr: Il faisait froid, et il n’avait jamais vu de neige.

s.t: He put his nose in the snow, and it was cold on his nose.
s.fr: Il enfonça le museau dans la neige, et le froid le saisit.

paras.summary: The boat reaches a cold place, and Buck steps onto the snow for the first time.

s.t: Many men and many dogs were in that place, and Buck saw a dog named Curly.
s.fr: Il y avait là beaucoup d’hommes et de chiens, et Buck remarqua une chienne nommée Curly.

s.t: Curly was a friendly dog, and she ran to a big wild dog to play.
s.fr: Curly était une chienne aimable, et elle courut jouer avec un grand chien sauvage.

s.t: The wild dog was thin and grey, and he did not want to play.
s.fr: Le chien sauvage était maigre et gris, et il n’avait aucune envie de jouer.

s.t: He jumped at Curly and cut her face with his teeth.
s.fr: Il bondit sur Curly et lui ouvrit le museau d’un coup de dents.

s.t: Buck was near her, but he did not move.
s.fr: Buck était tout près d’elle, mais il ne bougea pas.

paras.summary: In the crowded place a friendly dog named Curly runs to play with a thin grey wild dog, who cuts her face with his teeth.

s.t: More dogs came, and they stood around Curly in a ring.
s.fr: D’autres chiens accoururent et firent cercle autour de Curly.

s.t: They did not make a sound, and they did not move.
s.fr: Ils ne faisaient aucun bruit et ne bougeaient pas.

s.t: Curly jumped at the wild dog, but she fell down in the snow.
s.fr: Curly se jeta sur le chien sauvage, mais elle tomba dans la neige.

s.t: The dogs jumped on her, and in a moment she was dead.
s.fr: Les chiens se ruèrent sur elle, et en un instant elle était morte.

paras.summary: The other dogs stand silently around Curly, and when she falls in the snow they jump on her and kill her.

s.t: Buck saw it all, and he did not forget it.
s.fr: Buck avait tout vu, et il ne l’oublia pas.

s.t: "A dog must never fall down," Buck learned, "for the other dogs will kill him."
s.fr: « Un chien ne doit jamais tomber, comprit Buck, car les autres chiens le tueront. »

s.t: A man laughed, and Buck did not like the sound.
s.fr: Un homme éclata de rire, et Buck n’aima pas ce rire.

s.t: That was the law of the north, and Buck learned it well.
s.fr: C’était la loi du Nord, et Buck se la grava dans la mémoire.

s.t: That night he did not sleep.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, il ne ferma pas l’œil.

paras.summary: Buck learns that a dog must never fall down, because the other dogs will kill him, and a man laughs.

s.t: Next morning a man with a dark face came to the place and looked at Buck.
s.fr: Le lendemain matin, un homme au visage basané arriva et examina Buck.

s.t: His name was Perrault, and he carried letters for the government.
s.fr: Il s’appelait Perrault et portait les dépêches du gouvernement.

s.t: "This is a good dog," Perrault said, "for he is big and strong."
s.fr: « C’est un bon chien, dit Perrault, il est grand et fort. »

s.t: He gave money to the men, and they gave Buck to him.
s.fr: Il paya les hommes, qui lui cédèrent Buck.

paras.summary: A dark-faced man named Perrault, who carries letters for the government, looks at Buck, says he is a good dog, and buys him.

s.t: Perrault took Buck to a big man named Francois, who was waiting near a sled.
s.fr: Perrault conduisit Buck auprès d’un grand gaillard nommé François, qui attendait près d’un traîneau.

s.t: Francois looked at Buck for a long time.
s.fr: François considéra Buck un long moment.

s.t: "He is a very good dog," he said, "and he will pull well."
s.fr: « C’est un très bon chien, dit-il, et il tirera bien. »

s.t: "We must go north tonight," Perrault said, "for the letters are waiting."
s.fr: « Il faut partir pour le Nord dès ce soir, dit Perrault, car les dépêches attendent. »

paras.summary: Perrault takes Buck to a big man named Francois, who says Buck will pull well, and Perrault says they must go north because the letters are waiting.

s.t: By the sled there were two other dogs.
s.fr: Près du traîneau se tenaient deux autres chiens.

s.t: One was a big white dog named Spitz, and the other was a thin dog named Dave.
s.fr: L’un était un grand chien blanc nommé Spitz, l’autre un chien maigre nommé Dave.

s.t: Spitz came to Buck with a friendly face, but his eyes were cold.
s.fr: Spitz s’approcha de Buck d’un air aimable, mais ses yeux restaient froids.

s.t: Dave did not come, and he did not look at Buck.
s.fr: Dave ne vint pas, et il ne regarda même pas Buck.

s.t: Dave lay in the snow and slept.
s.fr: Dave dormait, couché dans la neige.

paras.summary: Two other dogs stand by the sled: a big white dog named Spitz, who looks friendly but has cold eyes, and a thin dog named Dave, who sleeps.

s.t: Buck stood still, and he did not like Spitz.
s.fr: Buck ne bougeait pas, et Spitz ne lui plaisait pas.

s.t: Spitz did not growl, and he did not bite, but he watched Buck.
s.fr: Spitz ne grondait pas, ne mordait pas, mais il surveillait Buck.

s.t: Buck watched him, and he remembered Curly.
s.fr: Buck le surveillait aussi, et il se souvenait de Curly.

s.t: A friendly face could be a wild dog's face.
s.fr: Sous un air aimable pouvait se cacher un chien sauvage.

paras.summary: Buck does not like Spitz, who watches him without growling, and remembers Curly, thinking that a friendly face can hide a wild dog.

s.t: Francois came with a harness in his hand.
s.fr: François arriva, un harnais à la main.

s.t: "Spitz is the best dog we have," he said to Perrault.
s.fr: « Spitz est le meilleur chien que nous ayons, » dit-il à Perrault.

s.t: "But he is a bad dog, too."
s.fr: « Mais c’est aussi une sale bête. »

s.t: "This new dog is strong," Perrault said, "but he has never seen the trail."
s.fr: « Ce nouveau chien est fort, dit Perrault, mais il n’a jamais vu la piste. »

paras.summary: Francois says Spitz is the best dog but a bad one, and Perrault says Buck is strong but has never seen the trail.

s.t: Francois put the harness on Buck, and it was made of leather.
s.fr: François passa à Buck un harnais de cuir.

s.t: Buck had never worn a harness, and he did not like it.
s.fr: Buck n’avait jamais porté de harnais, et cela ne lui plut pas.

s.t: "Stand still, dog," Francois said.
s.fr: « Tiens-toi tranquille, le chien, » dit François.

s.t: Buck stood still, for he remembered the club.
s.fr: Buck se tint tranquille, car il se souvenait du gourdin.

s.t: He looked at the sled, and he looked at the snow, and he did not know what to do.
s.fr: Il regarda le traîneau, puis la neige, sans savoir que faire.

s.t: Spitz watched all of this and did not make a sound.
s.fr: Spitz suivit toute la scène sans un bruit.

paras.summary: Francois puts a leather harness on Buck, who stands still because he remembers the club.

s.t: That evening the men made a fire and a tent, and the dogs lay near the sled.
s.fr: Ce soir-là, les hommes allumèrent un feu et dressèrent une tente, et les chiens se couchèrent près du traîneau.

s.t: Francois gave each dog a fish, and Buck was very hungry.
s.fr: François distribua un poisson à chaque chien, et Buck avait très faim.

s.t: The other dogs looked at his fish, and Buck ate it fast before they could take it.
s.fr: Les autres chiens lorgnaient son poisson, et Buck l’avala avant qu’ils ne puissent le lui prendre.

s.t: He had learned that a dog must eat fast in the north.
s.fr: Il avait appris que, dans le Nord, un chien doit manger vite.

s.t: "The dogs must eat," Perrault said, "or they cannot pull the sled."
s.fr: « Il faut que les chiens mangent, dit Perrault, sinon ils ne peuvent pas tirer le traîneau. »

paras.summary: The men make a fire and a tent, and Francois gives each dog a fish, and Buck eats his fast before the other dogs can take it.

s.t: Buck wanted to sleep by the fire, and he went to the tent.
s.fr: Buck voulut dormir près du feu et se dirigea vers la tente.

s.t: The men shouted at him, and they threw things at him.
s.fr: Les hommes l’accueillirent avec des cris et lui lancèrent tout ce qui leur tombait sous la main.

s.t: Buck ran away from the tent, and he did not know where to go.
s.fr: Buck s’enfuit loin de la tente, sans savoir où aller.

s.t: The wind was cold, and the snow came down.
s.fr: Un vent glacé soufflait, et la neige tombait.

paras.summary: Buck goes to the tent to sleep by the fire, but the men shout at him and throw things, so he runs away into the cold wind.

s.t: Buck lay down in the snow, but it was too cold.
s.fr: Buck se coucha dans la neige, mais il faisait bien trop froid.

s.t: He walked around the camp, and he did not see the other dogs.
s.fr: Il fit le tour du campement, mais les autres chiens avaient disparu.

s.t: He put his foot on the snow, and it broke, and he fell into a hole.
s.fr: Il posa la patte sur la neige, qui céda, et il tomba dans un trou.

s.t: Something moved under him, and Buck jumped up and growled.
s.fr: Quelque chose remua sous lui, et Buck bondit en grondant.

paras.summary: Buck cannot sleep in the cold snow, and when the snow breaks under his foot he falls into a hole where something moves.

s.t: It was Dave, and Dave did not growl.
s.fr: C’était Dave, qui ne gronda pas.

s.t: Dave was warm in his hole, and Buck saw that the other dogs were under the snow too.
s.fr: Dave avait chaud dans son trou, et Buck comprit que les autres chiens, eux aussi, dormaient sous la neige.

s.t: Each dog had made a hole, and each dog slept in it.
s.fr: Chaque chien s’était creusé un trou, et chacun y dormait.

s.t: Spitz was in a hole near Dave, and he watched Buck.
s.fr: Spitz, couché dans un trou près de Dave, surveillait Buck.

s.t: Buck did not like it, but he did not want to be cold.
s.fr: Cela ne plaisait pas à Buck, mais il ne voulait pas avoir froid.

paras.summary: Buck finds that the thing is Dave, and that all the other dogs sleep warm in holes under the snow.

s.t: Buck made a hole in the snow, and he dug it with his feet.
s.fr: Buck se creusa un trou dans la neige, à grands coups de pattes.

s.t: The hole was small, but it was warm, and Buck lay down in it.
s.fr: Le trou était petit, mais il y faisait chaud, et Buck s’y coucha.

s.t: He slept well that night, and the wind did not touch him.
s.fr: Il dormit bien cette nuit-là, à l’abri du vent.

s.t: Buck was learning fast, and the north was his teacher.
s.fr: Buck apprenait vite, et le Nord était son école.

s.t: In the morning Francois called the dogs, and Buck came out of the snow.
s.fr: Au matin, François appela les chiens, et Buck sortit de la neige.

s.t: The snow was over his back, and he shook it off.
s.fr: La neige lui recouvrait le dos ; il s’ébroua.

paras.summary: Buck digs his own hole in the snow, sleeps warm all night, and is learning fast.

s.t: The next day Francois put Buck in the harness, with Dave behind him and Spitz in front.
s.fr: Le lendemain, François attela Buck, Dave derrière lui et Spitz devant.

s.t: Spitz was the leader of the team, and he ran first on the trail.
s.fr: Spitz était le chef de l’attelage et courait en tête sur la piste.

s.t: Francois shouted a word, and the dogs pulled the sled over the snow.
s.fr: François lança un ordre, et les chiens entraînèrent le traîneau sur la neige.

s.t: Buck did not know how to pull, and the sled was very heavy.
s.fr: Buck ne savait pas tirer, et le traîneau pesait très lourd.

paras.summary: Buck is harnessed with Dave behind him and Spitz, the leader, in front, and when Francois shouts the dogs pull the heavy sled, though Buck does not know how.

s.t: When Buck made a mistake, Dave bit his legs.
s.fr: Quand Buck se trompait, Dave lui mordait les pattes.

s.t: Dave never growled, and he never said a word, but he bit Buck every time.
s.fr: Dave ne grondait jamais, ne disait jamais rien, mais il mordait Buck à chaque fois.

s.t: Buck learned to stop when the dogs stopped and to go when the dogs went.
s.fr: Buck apprit à s’arrêter quand les chiens s’arrêtaient et à repartir quand ils repartaient.

s.t: Spitz looked back at him and did not make a sound.
s.fr: Spitz se retourna pour le regarder, sans un bruit.

paras.summary: Dave bites Buck's legs each time he makes a mistake, and Buck learns to stop and go with the other dogs while Spitz looks back at him.

s.t: "Buck learns fast," Francois said to Perrault.
s.fr: « Buck apprend vite, » dit François à Perrault.

s.t: "He is a good dog," Perrault said, "and he is strong."
s.fr: « C’est un bon chien, dit Perrault, et il est fort. »

s.t: "Spitz is a good leader," Francois said, "and he leads the team well."
s.fr: « Spitz est un bon chef, dit François, et il mène bien l’attelage. »

s.t: The dogs ran all day, and the sun went down before the men stopped.
s.fr: Les chiens coururent toute la journée, et le soleil se coucha avant que les hommes ne fassent halte.

paras.summary: Francois and Perrault agree that Buck learns fast and is strong and that Spitz leads the team well, and the dogs run until the sun goes down.

s.t: Buck's feet hurt, and he was very tired, but he did not stop.
s.fr: Buck avait mal aux pattes, il était à bout de forces, mais il ne s’arrêta pas.

s.t: That night he ate his fish fast, and he dug a hole in the snow.
s.fr: Ce soir-là, il avala son poisson en hâte et creusa un trou dans la neige.

s.t: He slept, and in the morning he was in the harness again.
s.fr: Il dormit, et au matin il était de nouveau sous le harnais.

s.t: Each day he learned more, and each day he grew stronger.
s.fr: Chaque jour il en apprenait davantage, et chaque jour il devenait plus fort.

paras.summary: Buck's feet hurt and he is tired, but he eats fast, digs a hole, sleeps, and returns to the harness, learning more and growing stronger each day.

s.t: After some days Perrault brought two more dogs to the team.
s.fr: Au bout de quelques jours, Perrault amena deux nouveaux chiens à l’attelage.

s.t: They were brothers named Billee and Joe, and both of them were big and strong.
s.fr: C’étaient deux frères, Billee et Joe, grands et forts l’un comme l’autre.

s.t: Billee was a friendly dog, and he wanted to be friends with every dog.
s.fr: Billee était un chien aimable, qui voulait être l’ami de tous.

s.t: Joe was angry, and he growled at every dog he saw.
s.fr: Joe était hargneux et grondait contre tous les chiens qu’il croisait.

s.t: Spitz did not like Billee or Joe, and he bit them when the men could not see.
s.fr: Spitz n’aimait ni Billee ni Joe, et il les mordait dès que les hommes avaient le dos tourné.

paras.summary: Perrault brings two more dogs, the brothers Billee, who is friendly, and Joe, who is angry, and Spitz bites them when the men cannot see.

s.t: The trail went over a river, and the ice on the river was thick.
s.fr: La piste traversait une rivière, couverte d’une épaisse couche de glace.

s.t: The dogs pulled the sled over the ice, and the wind was cold on their faces.
s.fr: Les chiens tiraient le traîneau sur la glace, et le vent glacé leur fouettait le museau.

s.t: At night they slept in holes in the snow, and Buck was not cold.
s.fr: La nuit, ils dormaient dans des trous creusés dans la neige, et Buck n’avait pas froid.

s.t: Buck liked the trail, for it made him strong.
s.fr: Buck aimait la piste, car elle l’endurcissait.

paras.summary: The trail crosses a thick frozen river in the cold wind, the dogs sleep in holes at night, and Buck likes the trail for making him strong.

s.t: Buck was always hungry, for the fish was small.
s.fr: Buck avait toujours faim, car sa ration de poisson était bien maigre.

s.t: Perrault had meat in a sack near the tent, and Buck watched the sack.
s.fr: Perrault gardait de la viande dans un sac près de la tente, et Buck ne quittait pas ce sac des yeux.

s.t: One morning no man saw Buck, and he took some meat and ran away with it.
s.fr: Un matin, profitant de ce que personne ne le voyait, Buck déroba un morceau de viande et s’enfuit avec.

s.t: He ate it fast in the snow, and no one knew that he had taken it.
s.fr: Il la dévora dans la neige, et nul ne sut qu’il l’avait prise.

s.t: Buck did not feel bad about it, for a dog in the north must eat or die.
s.fr: Buck n’en éprouva aucun remords, car dans le Nord un chien doit manger ou mourir.

s.t: Buck had learned to steal.
s.fr: Buck avait appris à voler.

paras.summary: Buck is always hungry, and one morning when no man sees him he steals some meat from Perrault's sack and eats it fast in the snow.

s.t: That night Perrault looked in the sack, and some of the meat was gone.
s.fr: Ce soir-là, Perrault jeta un coup d’œil dans le sac : il manquait de la viande.

s.t: "A dog has taken the meat," Perrault said.
s.fr: « Un chien a pris la viande, » dit Perrault.

s.t: "Who took it?" Francois asked.
s.fr: « Qui l’a prise ? » demanda François.

s.t: "I do not know," Perrault said, "but I will find him."
s.fr: « Je ne sais pas, dit Perrault, mais je le trouverai. »

s.t: A dog named Dub stole meat too, but Dub was slow, and the men caught him.
s.fr: Un chien nommé Dub volait aussi de la viande, mais Dub était lent, et les hommes le prirent sur le fait.

s.t: Francois hit Dub, and Dub fell down in the snow.
s.fr: François frappa Dub, qui roula dans la neige.

s.t: "That dog is a thief," Perrault said, "and he will not steal again."
s.fr: « Ce chien est un voleur, dit Perrault, et il ne volera plus. »

paras.summary: Perrault finds meat gone, and a slow dog named Dub steals too and is caught and hit by Francois.

s.t: Buck saw it, and he learned that a thief must be clever.
s.fr: Buck vit tout, et il comprit qu’un voleur doit être rusé.

s.t: In the north a clever thief got food, and a slow thief was hit.
s.fr: Dans le Nord, le voleur rusé mangeait, et le voleur lent recevait des coups.

s.t: The days were very cold, and the snow was deep, but Buck grew strong.
s.fr: Le froid était mordant, la neige profonde, mais Buck prenait des forces.

s.t: His feet were thick and big, and many dogs died in the snow.
s.fr: Ses pattes s’étaient élargies et endurcies, tandis que beaucoup de chiens mouraient dans la neige.

s.t: He knew every sound in the night, and he was more like a wild dog now.
s.fr: Il connaissait tous les bruits de la nuit, et il ressemblait désormais davantage à un chien sauvage.

s.t: He was a big dog from a farm, but the farm was far away.
s.fr: C’était un grand chien venu d’une ferme, mais cette ferme était bien loin.

paras.summary: Buck learns that a thief in the north must be clever, and he grows strong and more like a wild dog, far from the farm.

s.t: At night Buck lay by the fire and dreamed.
s.fr: La nuit, Buck s’étendait près du feu et rêvait.

s.t: In his dream he saw a hairy man who sat by a fire in the dark.
s.fr: Dans son rêve, il voyait un homme velu assis auprès d’un feu, dans les ténèbres.

s.t: The man was afraid of the dark, and he slept with his head on his knees.
s.fr: L’homme avait peur du noir, et il dormait la tête sur les genoux.

s.t: Around the fire the dark was full of eyes, and the eyes looked at the man.
s.fr: Autour du feu, les ténèbres fourmillaient d’yeux qui fixaient l’homme.

s.t: Buck did not forget the dream.
s.fr: Buck n’oublia pas ce rêve.

paras.summary: At night by the fire Buck dreams of a hairy man who sits afraid in the dark, and he does not forget the dream.

s.t: The days were short, and the nights were long, and the snow was deep on the trail.
s.fr: Les jours étaient courts, les nuits longues, et la neige s’amoncelait sur la piste.

s.t: The dogs ran from morning until night, and Perrault and Francois ran beside the sled.
s.fr: Les chiens couraient du matin au soir, et Perrault et François couraient à côté du traîneau.

s.t: "We must reach Dawson soon," Perrault said, "for the letters are late."
s.fr: « Il faut gagner Dawson au plus vite, dit Perrault, car les dépêches sont en retard. »

s.t: "The dogs are tired," Francois said, "but they will run."
s.fr: « Les chiens sont fatigués, dit François, mais ils courront. »

paras.summary: The days are short and the snow deep as the dogs run from morning until night, and Perrault says they must reach Dawson soon because the letters are late.

s.t: Each day Spitz looked at Buck with cold eyes, and each day Buck looked back.
s.fr: Chaque jour, Spitz posait sur Buck ses yeux froids, et chaque jour Buck lui rendait son regard.

s.t: Spitz was the leader, and he did not want another dog to be strong.
s.fr: Spitz était le chef, et il ne tolérait pas qu’un autre chien devienne fort.

s.t: Buck did not want to fight, but he did not run away from Spitz.
s.fr: Buck ne cherchait pas la bagarre, mais il ne reculait pas devant Spitz.

s.t: Buck knew that the two of them would fight one day.
s.fr: Buck savait qu’un jour ils se battraient tous deux.

paras.summary: Spitz, the leader, looks at Buck with cold eyes each day, and Buck looks back, knowing that the two of them will fight one day.

s.t: One evening Dub did not run fast, and Spitz jumped at him.
s.fr: Un soir, Dub ne courut pas assez vite, et Spitz se jeta sur lui.

s.t: Dub fell down in the snow, and Spitz stood over him with his teeth ready.
s.fr: Dub roula dans la neige, et Spitz se campa au-dessus de lui, les crocs découverts.

s.t: Buck ran to them, and he stood between Spitz and Dub.
s.fr: Buck accourut et se plaça entre Spitz et Dub.

s.t: Spitz looked at Buck, and Buck looked at Spitz, and neither dog moved.
s.fr: Spitz regarda Buck, Buck regarda Spitz, et ni l’un ni l’autre ne bougea.

paras.summary: One evening Spitz jumps at slow Dub, but Buck stands between them, and neither Spitz nor Buck moves.

s.t: Francois saw it, and he came with his whip in his hand.
s.fr: François vit la scène et accourut, le fouet à la main.

s.t: "Spitz will not hit that dog again," he said.
s.fr: « Spitz ne touchera plus à ce chien, » dit-il.

s.t: Spitz went back to his place in the team, but he did not forget.
s.fr: Spitz regagna sa place dans l’attelage, mais il n’oublia pas.

s.t: That night Spitz did not sleep, and he watched Buck from his hole.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, Spitz ne dormit pas : de son trou, il surveillait Buck.

paras.summary: Francois comes with his whip, and Spitz goes back to his place but does not forget and watches Buck all night.

s.t: "Those two dogs will fight," Francois said to Perrault.
s.fr: « Ces deux chiens vont se battre, » dit François à Perrault.

s.t: "Buck is a good dog," Perrault said, "and he is not afraid of Spitz."
s.fr: « Buck est un bon chien, dit Perrault, et il n’a pas peur de Spitz. »

s.t: "Spitz is the leader," Francois said, "and he will not give up his place."
s.fr: « Spitz est le chef, dit François, et il ne cédera pas sa place. »

s.t: "Then one of them must die," Perrault said.
s.fr: « Alors l’un des deux devra mourir, » dit Perrault.

paras.summary: Francois and Perrault agree that Buck and Spitz will fight and that one of them must die.

s.t: Buck heard the men, but he did not know their words.
s.fr: Buck entendait les hommes, mais il ne comprenait pas leurs paroles.

s.t: He knew only that a fight was coming, and he was ready.
s.fr: Il savait seulement qu’un combat approchait, et il était prêt.

s.t: He dug a hole in the snow and lay down, but he did not sleep.
s.fr: Il se creusa un trou dans la neige et s’y coucha, mais sans dormir.

s.t: The wind was cold, and the stars were bright over the snow.
s.fr: Le vent était glacé, et les étoiles brillaient au-dessus de la neige.

paras.summary: Buck does not understand the men's words, but he knows a fight is coming, and he lies awake in his hole.

s.t: One night the men made camp by a lake, and the moon was bright over the snow.
s.fr: Une nuit, les hommes dressèrent le campement au bord d’un lac ; la lune brillait sur la neige.

s.t: The dogs lay in their holes, and the men slept in the tent.
s.fr: Les chiens étaient couchés dans leurs trous, et les hommes dormaient sous la tente.

s.t: A rabbit jumped up from the snow, and it ran across the lake.
s.fr: Un lièvre jaillit de la neige et fila à travers le lac.

s.t: Every dog heard it, and every dog jumped up and ran after it.
s.fr: Tous les chiens l’entendirent, et tous bondirent à sa poursuite.

paras.summary: One bright night by a lake a rabbit jumps up from the snow, and every dog runs after it.

s.t: Spitz ran first, and Buck ran behind him, with the other dogs behind Buck.
s.fr: Spitz menait la course, Buck sur ses talons, et les autres chiens derrière Buck.

s.t: The rabbit ran around a bend, and Spitz cut across the snow to catch it.
s.fr: Le lièvre disparut dans un tournant, et Spitz coupa à travers la neige pour le rattraper.

s.t: Buck did not follow the rabbit, and he did not cut across the snow.
s.fr: Buck, lui, ne suivit pas le lièvre et ne coupa pas non plus à travers la neige.

s.t: He jumped at Spitz, and both dogs rolled over in the snow.
s.fr: Il bondit sur Spitz, et les deux chiens roulèrent dans la neige.

paras.summary: Spitz leads the chase and cuts across a bend, but Buck jumps at him, and both dogs roll over in the snow.

s.t: Spitz got up fast, and he bit Buck's shoulder.
s.fr: Spitz se releva d’un bond et mordit Buck à l’épaule.

s.t: The other dogs came and stood in a ring around the two of them.
s.fr: Les autres chiens arrivèrent et firent cercle autour d’eux.

s.t: They did not make a sound, and they watched with their eyes bright in the moon.
s.fr: Ils ne faisaient aucun bruit et regardaient, les yeux brillants sous la lune.

s.t: Buck knew that this was the fight, and he knew that one of them must die.
s.fr: Buck savait que l’heure du combat était venue, et que l’un des deux devait mourir.

paras.summary: Spitz bites Buck's shoulder, and the other dogs make a silent ring around them, and Buck knows that one of them must die.

s.t: Spitz was bigger than Buck, and he had fought many times before.
s.fr: Spitz était plus grand que Buck, et il s’était déjà battu bien des fois.

s.t: He bit at Buck's throat, but Buck jumped away, and he bit again and again.
s.fr: Il chercha la gorge de Buck, mais Buck fit un bond de côté, et Spitz mordit encore et encore.

s.t: Buck was clever, and he did not go near Spitz's teeth.
s.fr: Buck était rusé, et il se tenait hors de portée des crocs de Spitz.

s.t: Blood ran from both dogs, and the snow was red.
s.fr: Les deux chiens saignaient, et la neige rougissait.

s.t: He waited, and at last he saw his chance.
s.fr: Il attendit, et enfin l’occasion se présenta.

paras.summary: Spitz is bigger and has fought many times, but Buck jumps away from his teeth and waits until he sees his chance.

s.t: Buck jumped at Spitz's front leg, and he broke it with his teeth.
s.fr: Buck se jeta sur la patte avant de Spitz et la lui brisa d’un coup de dents.

s.t: Spitz fell down in the snow, and he could not get up.
s.fr: Spitz s’effondra dans la neige, incapable de se relever.

s.t: The ring of dogs came closer, and Spitz looked at Buck.
s.fr: Le cercle des chiens se resserra, et Spitz leva les yeux vers Buck.

s.t: Buck stood over him, and the other dogs waited.
s.fr: Buck se dressait au-dessus de lui, et les autres chiens attendaient.

paras.summary: Buck breaks Spitz's front leg, Spitz falls and cannot get up, and the ring of dogs closes in.

s.t: Spitz was dead in a moment, and the dogs stood over him.
s.fr: En un instant, Spitz était mort, et les chiens se tenaient au-dessus de son corps.

s.t: Buck stood in the moon and looked at the ring of dogs.
s.fr: Buck, sous la lune, contemplait le cercle des chiens.

s.t: He was the master now, and the fight was over.
s.fr: C’était lui le maître désormais, et le combat était fini.

s.t: Later the men came from the tent, and they saw the dogs in the snow.
s.fr: Plus tard, les hommes sortirent de la tente et virent les chiens dans la neige.

s.t: Francois looked at Spitz, and then he looked at Buck.
s.fr: François regarda Spitz, puis Buck.

paras.summary: Spitz dies, and Buck stands in the moonlight as the master of the team.

s.t: In the morning Francois called Spitz, but Spitz did not come.
s.fr: Au matin, François appela Spitz, mais Spitz ne vint pas.

s.t: He saw blood in the snow, and he saw the wounds on Buck.
s.fr: Il vit du sang sur la neige et les blessures de Buck.

s.t: "Spitz is dead," Francois said.
s.fr: « Spitz est mort, » dit François.

s.t: "Buck fought him, and Buck won."
s.fr: « Buck s’est battu avec lui, et c’est Buck qui a gagné. »

s.t: Perrault looked at the snow for a long time.
s.fr: Perrault resta longtemps à regarder la neige.

paras.summary: In the morning Francois calls Spitz, but he sees blood in the snow and the wounds on Buck, and says that Buck fought Spitz and won.

s.t: "Spitz fought well," Perrault said, "but Buck fought better."
s.fr: « Spitz s’est bien battu, dit Perrault, mais Buck s’est battu mieux encore. »

s.t: Francois took the harness to Solleks, an old strong dog, and he put it on him.
s.fr: François apporta le harnais à Solleks, un vieux chien encore plein de force, et le lui passa.

s.t: "Solleks will be the leader now," he said.
s.fr: « Désormais, c’est Solleks qui sera le chef, » dit-il.

s.t: But Buck went to the front of the team and stood in Spitz's place.
s.fr: Mais Buck alla se poster en tête de l’attelage, à la place de Spitz.

paras.summary: Perrault says Buck fought better, and Francois harnesses Solleks as the new leader, but Buck goes to the front and stands in Spitz's place.

s.t: "Go away, Buck," Francois said.
s.fr: « Va-t’en, Buck, » dit François.

s.t: Buck did not move, and he looked at Francois.
s.fr: Buck ne bougea pas et fixa François.

s.t: Francois took a club, and Buck stepped back, but he did not go to his place.
s.fr: François prit un gourdin ; Buck recula, mais sans regagner sa place.

s.t: "The dog wants that place," Perrault said, "and he has won it."
s.fr: « Ce chien veut cette place, dit Perrault, et il l’a gagnée. »

paras.summary: Buck refuses to leave Spitz's place even when Francois takes a club, and Perrault says Buck has won the place.

s.t: Francois put the harness on Buck, and Buck stood in front of the team.
s.fr: François passa le harnais à Buck, qui prit la tête de l’attelage.

s.t: Solleks went to the back, and he did not growl.
s.fr: Solleks passa à l’arrière sans gronder.

s.t: "Go!" Francois shouted.
s.fr: « En route ! » cria François.

s.t: The dogs pulled the sled, and Buck ran first.
s.fr: Les chiens tirèrent le traîneau, et Buck courut en tête.

s.t: He ran faster than Spitz.
s.fr: Il courait plus vite que Spitz.

paras.summary: Francois puts the harness on Buck and puts him in front, Solleks goes to the back, and Buck leads the team faster than Spitz did.

s.t: Buck was a better leader than Spitz, for he was clever and strong.
s.fr: Buck était un meilleur chef que Spitz, car il était rusé et fort.

s.t: He made the other dogs work, and he did not let them stop.
s.fr: Il faisait travailler les autres chiens et ne leur laissait aucun répit.

s.t: The team ran faster each day, and they came to Dawson before the letters were late.
s.fr: L’attelage gagnait en vitesse de jour en jour, et ils atteignirent Dawson avant que les dépêches ne soient en retard.

s.t: "That is the best team in the north," Perrault said.
s.fr: « C’est le meilleur attelage du Nord, » dit Perrault.

paras.summary: Buck proves a better leader than Spitz, making the other dogs work, and the team reaches Dawson before the letters are late.

s.t: Dawson was a town of houses and tents, and many men and many dogs were in the streets.
s.fr: Dawson était une ville de maisons et de tentes, et les rues grouillaient d’hommes et de chiens.

s.t: Many of the men came to look at the team, and they looked at Buck.
s.fr: Beaucoup d’hommes vinrent voir l’attelage, et tous les regards se portèrent sur Buck.

s.t: "That leader is the best dog I have seen," one man said.
s.fr: « Le chien de tête, là, c’est le meilleur que j’aie jamais vu, » dit un homme.

s.t: "He is big and strong," another man said, "and he is clever."
s.fr: « Il est grand et fort, dit un autre, et rusé, avec ça. »

s.t: Perrault was glad, and he gave Buck extra meat that night.
s.fr: Perrault, ravi, offrit ce soir-là à Buck une double ration de viande.

paras.summary: At Dawson many men come to look at the team and say Buck is the best dog they have seen, and Perrault gives him extra meat.

s.t: Perrault took new letters, and in two days the team started back on the trail.
s.fr: Perrault se chargea de nouvelles dépêches, et deux jours plus tard l’attelage reprenait la piste du retour.

s.t: Buck led the team, and the dogs obeyed him.
s.fr: Buck menait l’attelage, et les chiens lui obéissaient.

s.t: Dave pulled behind him, and Solleks pulled in front of the sled.
s.fr: Dave tirait derrière lui, et Solleks tirait juste devant le traîneau.

s.t: Buck was proud of the team, and he was proud of himself.
s.fr: Buck était fier de son attelage, et fier de lui-même.

paras.summary: Perrault takes new letters, and the team starts back with Buck leading, Dave and Solleks behind him, and Buck proud of the team.

s.t: The team came back to Skagway, and there Perrault and Francois had new work.
s.fr: L’attelage revint à Skagway, où de nouveaux ordres attendaient Perrault et François.

s.t: They must go to a new place, and they could not take the dogs.
s.fr: Ils devaient partir ailleurs et ne pouvaient pas emmener les chiens.

s.t: Francois said goodbye to Buck, and he went away with Perrault.
s.fr: François fit ses adieux à Buck, puis il s’en alla avec Perrault.

s.t: Buck never saw them again.
s.fr: Buck ne les revit jamais.

paras.summary: The team returns to Skagway, where Perrault and Francois have new work and must leave the dogs, and Buck never sees them again.

s.t: A new man came and bought the team, and he had a hard face.
s.fr: Un autre homme, au visage dur, vint acheter l’attelage.

s.t: He drove the mail sled, and he carried letters for the men who dug for gold.
s.fr: Il conduisait le traîneau du courrier et portait les lettres des chercheurs d’or.

s.t: "We will start tomorrow," he said, "and we will not stop."
s.fr: « Nous partirons demain, dit-il, et nous ne nous arrêterons pas. »

s.t: The sled was heavier than the old sled, and Buck knew that the work would be hard.
s.fr: Le traîneau était plus lourd que l’ancien, et Buck comprit que le travail serait rude.

paras.summary: A new man with a hard face buys the team to drive the mail sled, saying they will start tomorrow and not stop, and Buck knows the work will be hard.

s.t: Every day the dogs pulled the heavy sled over the snow, and the day was long.
s.fr: Chaque jour, les chiens tiraient le lourd traîneau sur la neige, et les journées n’en finissaient pas.

s.t: They ran until night, and then they ate a little fish and slept in the snow.
s.fr: Ils couraient jusqu’à la nuit, puis mangeaient un peu de poisson et dormaient dans la neige.

s.t: In the morning they were tired, but the man put them in the harness again.
s.fr: Le matin, ils étaient encore fatigués, mais l’homme les attelait de nouveau.

s.t: The dogs grew thin, and their feet hurt, and no dog rested.
s.fr: Les chiens maigrissaient, leurs pattes les faisaient souffrir, et aucun ne connaissait de repos.

s.t: The man did not talk to the dogs, and he did not look at them.
s.fr: L’homme ne parlait pas aux chiens ; il ne les regardait même pas.

s.t: Some dogs fell down in the snow, and the man hit them until they got up.
s.fr: Certains chiens s’écroulaient dans la neige, et l’homme les frappait jusqu’à ce qu’ils se relèvent.

s.t: Buck saw the dogs fall, and he was afraid that Dave would fall too.
s.fr: Buck voyait les chiens tomber, et il craignait que Dave ne tombe à son tour.

paras.summary: Every day the dogs pull the heavy sled until night, eat little, sleep in the snow, and are put back in the harness tired and thin, and the man hits the dogs that fall.

s.t: Each night the man fed the dogs, and each night the dogs were hungry.
s.fr: Chaque soir, l’homme nourrissait les chiens, et chaque soir ils restaient affamés.

s.t: "You must be strong tomorrow," the man said.
s.fr: « Demain, il faudra être forts, » disait l’homme.

s.t: The dogs ate, but the fish was small, and they were still hungry.
s.fr: Les chiens mangeaient, mais le poisson était petit, et ils avaient encore faim.

s.t: Buck watched Dave, and Dave watched Buck, and neither dog made a sound.
s.fr: Buck regardait Dave, Dave regardait Buck, et ni l’un ni l’autre ne faisait aucun bruit.

paras.summary: Each night the man feeds the hungry dogs a small fish and says they must be strong tomorrow, and Buck and Dave watch each other.

s.t: Buck did not stop, for he was the leader, and the team ran behind him.
s.fr: Buck ne s’arrêtait pas, car il était le chef, et l’attelage courait derrière lui.

s.t: He pulled hard, and he did not think about the work.
s.fr: Il tirait de toutes ses forces, sans penser à sa peine.

s.t: But Dave was not well, and Buck saw that he was sick.
s.fr: Mais Dave n’allait pas bien, et Buck vit qu’il était malade.

s.t: Dave did not eat his fish, and he walked with his head down.
s.fr: Dave ne touchait plus à son poisson, et il marchait la tête basse.

paras.summary: Buck keeps leading the team and pulling hard, but he sees that Dave is sick, does not eat, and walks with his head down.

s.t: Dave grew more sick each day, and one morning he cried out when the sled began to move.
s.fr: Dave allait de plus en plus mal, et un matin il poussa un cri quand le traîneau s’ébranla.

s.t: The man came and looked at Dave for a long time.
s.fr: L’homme vint examiner Dave un long moment.

s.t: "That dog is sick," the man said, "and he cannot pull the sled."
s.fr: « Ce chien est malade, dit l’homme, et il ne peut plus tirer le traîneau. »

s.t: He took Dave out of the harness and put Solleks in his place.
s.fr: Il détela Dave et mit Solleks à sa place.

paras.summary: Dave grows sicker until he cries out when the sled moves, and the man says he cannot pull and puts Solleks in his place.

s.t: Dave did not want to leave his place, for pulling the sled was his work.
s.fr: Dave ne voulait pas quitter sa place, car tirer le traîneau, c’était son métier.

s.t: He ran beside the sled in the deep snow, and he bit at Solleks and tried to take his place back.
s.fr: Il courait à côté du traîneau dans la neige profonde, et il s’en prenait à Solleks à coups de dents pour tenter de reprendre sa place.

s.t: The man hit Dave with his whip, but Dave did not stop.
s.fr: L’homme cingla Dave de son fouet, mais Dave ne renonça pas.

s.t: At last the man let Dave into the harness again.
s.fr: Enfin, l’homme laissa Dave reprendre sa place sous le harnais.

paras.summary: Dave runs beside the sled and bites at Solleks to take his place back, and the man finally puts him in the harness again.

s.t: Dave pulled all day, but he was very weak, and he fell down many times.
s.fr: Dave tira toute la journée, mais il était très faible et tomba bien des fois.

s.t: Each time he got up, and each time he pulled again.
s.fr: Chaque fois il se releva, et chaque fois il se remit à tirer.

s.t: That night he lay in the snow and did not eat his fish.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, il resta couché dans la neige sans toucher à son poisson.

s.t: In the morning he could not stand, and he looked at Buck with sad eyes.
s.fr: Au matin, il ne put se tenir debout, et il leva vers Buck des yeux tristes.

paras.summary: Dave pulls all day though he is weak and falls many times, and that night he does not eat, and in the morning he cannot stand.

s.t: The man stopped the sled and took out a gun.
s.fr: L’homme arrêta le traîneau et sortit un fusil.

s.t: Buck did not want to look at Dave, but he could not look away from him.
s.fr: Buck ne voulait pas regarder Dave, mais il ne pouvait en détacher les yeux.

s.t: The man said nothing, and the dogs stood in the snow.
s.fr: L’homme ne dit rien, et les chiens restaient plantés dans la neige.

s.t: The team went on, and Buck heard the gun behind him.
s.fr: L’attelage repartit, et Buck entendit le coup de feu derrière lui.

s.t: No one spoke, and the man came back to the sled and did not say a word.
s.fr: Personne ne parla, et l’homme revint au traîneau sans dire un mot.

paras.summary: The man stops the sled and takes out a gun, and the team goes on, and Buck hears the gun and the man comes back without a word.

s.t: That was the end of Dave, and Buck did not forget him.
s.fr: Ce fut la fin de Dave, et Buck ne l’oublia pas.

s.t: Buck missed Dave, for Dave had taught him the trail.
s.fr: Dave manquait à Buck, car c’était lui qui lui avait appris la piste.

s.t: The wind blew across the snow, and the cold was very great.
s.fr: Le vent balayait la neige, et il gelait à pierre fendre.

s.t: He pulled the sled all that day, and the next day, and the day after.
s.fr: Il tira le traîneau toute cette journée, puis le lendemain, puis le surlendemain.

s.t: He was thin and tired, but he did not stop, for he was the leader.
s.fr: Il était maigre et épuisé, mais il ne s’arrêtait pas, car il était le chef.

s.t: Solleks pulled behind him, and Solleks was old and slow.
s.fr: Derrière lui tirait Solleks, vieux et lent.

paras.summary: Dave is gone, and Buck does not forget him, and he leads the tired team on day after day.

s.t: At last the man sold the tired team to Hal, Charles and Mercedes.
s.fr: Enfin, l’homme vendit l’attelage épuisé à Hal, Charles et Mercedes.

s.t: Mercedes was the wife of Charles, and Hal was a big man who talked all the time.
s.fr: Mercedes était la femme de Charles, et Hal un grand gaillard qui parlait sans arrêt.

s.t: They came from a warm place, and they knew nothing about the snow.
s.fr: Ils venaient d’un pays chaud et ne connaissaient rien à la neige.

s.t: Buck looked at them, and he did not like them.
s.fr: Buck les regarda, et ils ne lui plurent pas.

paras.summary: The man sells the tired team to Hal, Charles and Mercedes, who come from a warm place and know nothing about snow, and Buck does not like them.

s.t: Hal had a big gun, and Charles was slow.
s.fr: Hal portait un gros fusil, et Charles était lent.

s.t: Mercedes cried when the men did not do what she wanted.
s.fr: Mercedes fondait en larmes dès que les hommes ne faisaient pas ce qu’elle voulait.

s.t: Their tent was bad, and everything they had lay on the ground.
s.fr: Leur tente ne valait rien, et toutes leurs affaires traînaient par terre.

s.t: They did not know how to put their things in the sled.
s.fr: Ils ne savaient pas charger un traîneau.

paras.summary: Hal has a big gun, Charles is slow, Mercedes cries when the men do not do what she wants, and their things lie on the ground.

s.t: They put more things in the sled than the dogs could pull.
s.fr: Ils entassèrent sur le traîneau plus de bagages que les chiens n’en pouvaient tirer.

s.t: Another man watched them, and he laughed.
s.fr: Un autre homme les regardait faire en riant.

s.t: "You cannot take all that," he said.
s.fr: « Vous ne pouvez pas emporter tout ça, » dit-il.

s.t: "The dogs cannot pull it."
s.fr: « Les chiens ne pourront pas tirer ça. »

s.t: "We can take it," Hal said, "for we have many dogs."
s.fr: « Nous l’emporterons, dit Hal, nous avons bien assez de chiens. »

paras.summary: They put more in the sled than the dogs can pull, and a man says they cannot take it all, but Hal says they can.

s.t: "The dogs are tired," the man said, "and they need rest."
s.fr: « Les chiens sont épuisés, dit l’homme, ils ont besoin de repos. »

s.t: "We do not need your help," Hal said.
s.fr: « Nous n’avons que faire de votre aide, » dit Hal.

s.t: "We know what we are doing," Charles said.
s.fr: « Nous savons ce que nous faisons, » dit Charles.

s.t: "You do not know," the man said.
s.fr: « Vous n’en savez rien, » dit l’homme.

paras.summary: The man says the dogs need rest, but Hal and Charles say they do not need help.

s.t: Hal put many dogs in the harness, and Buck was the leader.
s.fr: Hal attela une foule de chiens, avec Buck en tête.

s.t: The other dogs were thin, and they did not know the trail.
s.fr: Les autres chiens étaient maigres et ne connaissaient pas la piste.

s.t: Mercedes sat on the sled, and she did not want to walk.
s.fr: Mercedes s’installa sur le traîneau : elle ne voulait pas marcher.

s.t: "Go!" Hal shouted.
s.fr: « En route ! » cria Hal.

s.t: He hit the dogs with his whip, and they pulled.
s.fr: Il fouetta les chiens, qui tirèrent.

paras.summary: Hal harnesses many dogs with Buck as leader, Mercedes sits on the sled, and Hal shouts and whips the dogs.

s.t: The sled did not move, for it was too heavy.
s.fr: Le traîneau ne bougea pas : il était trop lourd.

s.t: Hal hit the dogs again and again, and Buck pulled as hard as he could.
s.fr: Hal frappa les chiens encore et encore, et Buck tira de toutes ses forces.

s.t: At last the sled moved a little, and then it fell over in the snow.
s.fr: Enfin le traîneau avança un peu, puis il se renversa dans la neige.

s.t: Everything fell out on the ground, and the men laughed.
s.fr: Tout le chargement se répandit sur le sol, et les hommes éclatèrent de rire.

s.t: "Take half of it out," the man said, "or the dogs will die."
s.fr: « Enlevez-en la moitié, dit l’homme, ou vos chiens vont crever. »

s.t: Hal did not want to listen, but Charles took some things out of the sled.
s.fr: Hal ne voulait rien entendre, mais Charles retira quelques affaires du traîneau.

s.t: The man shook his head and went away, for he knew that these three would not go far.
s.fr: L’homme secoua la tête et s’éloigna : il savait que ces trois-là n’iraient pas loin.

paras.summary: The dogs cannot move the heavy sled until Hal whips them, and then it falls over, and the man says to take half out or the dogs will die, and Charles takes some things out.

s.t: The team went slowly, and each day it went more slowly.
s.fr: L’attelage avançait lentement, et chaque jour plus lentement encore.

s.t: Hal gave the dogs a little fish, and he said that they did not need more.
s.fr: Hal donnait aux chiens un peu de poisson, et prétendait qu’il ne leur en fallait pas davantage.

s.t: "They will run on a little fish," he said, "and we will buy more food at Dawson."
s.fr: « Un peu de poisson leur suffira pour courir, dit-il, et nous achèterons des vivres à Dawson. »

s.t: But Dawson was far away, and the fish was soon gone.
s.fr: Mais Dawson était loin, et il n’y eut bientôt plus de poisson.

paras.summary: The team goes more slowly each day, and Hal feeds the dogs a little fish, saying they will buy more at Dawson, but the fish is soon gone.

s.t: The dogs were very hungry, and they were very weak.
s.fr: Les chiens mouraient de faim et n’avaient plus de forces.

s.t: Dub fell down in the snow, and he did not get up.
s.fr: Dub tomba dans la neige et ne se releva pas.

s.t: Billee died, and then Joe died, and the men left them behind on the trail.
s.fr: Billee mourut, puis ce fut le tour de Joe, et les hommes les abandonnèrent sur la piste.

s.t: Buck and three other dogs were still alive.
s.fr: Il ne restait plus en vie que Buck et trois autres chiens.

paras.summary: The starving dogs grow weak, Dub, Billee and Joe die and are left behind, and only Buck and three other dogs remain.

s.t: Hal and Charles were angry with each other every day, and Mercedes cried.
s.fr: Hal et Charles se querellaient tous les jours, et Mercedes pleurait.

s.t: "You are a fool," Hal said to Charles.
s.fr: « Tu es un imbécile, » dit Hal à Charles.

s.t: "You are the fool," Charles said to Hal, "for you did not buy food."
s.fr: « L’imbécile, c’est toi, répondit Charles, puisque tu n’as pas acheté de vivres. »

s.t: Mercedes cried more, and she said that both men were bad.
s.fr: Mercedes pleura de plus belle et déclara que les deux hommes étaient méchants.

paras.summary: Hal and Charles are angry every day and call each other fools, and Mercedes cries and says both men are bad.

s.t: Mercedes was tired, and she sat on the sled again.
s.fr: Lasse de marcher, Mercedes se rassit sur le traîneau.

s.t: She was heavy, and the sled was heavier, and the dogs could hardly pull it.
s.fr: Elle était lourde, le traîneau s’en trouvait alourdi, et les chiens parvenaient à peine à le tirer.

s.t: "Get off the sled," Charles said, "for the dogs will die."
s.fr: « Descends du traîneau, dit Charles, ou les chiens vont mourir. »

s.t: Mercedes said that she would not walk, for her feet hurt.
s.fr: Mercedes répondit qu’elle ne marcherait pas, car elle avait mal aux pieds.

paras.summary: Mercedes sits on the sled again, though Charles says the dogs will die, and says she will not walk because her feet hurt.

s.t: In many camps the men looked at the thin dogs.
s.fr: Dans bien des campements, les hommes regardaient les chiens efflanqués.

s.t: Some men said nothing, and some men shook their heads.
s.fr: Certains ne disaient rien, d’autres secouaient la tête.

s.t: "They will not live," one man said.
s.fr: « Ils n’en ont plus pour longtemps, » dit un homme.

s.t: "They will not come to Dawson," said another.
s.fr: « Ils n’arriveront jamais à Dawson, » dit un autre.

paras.summary: Men in the camps shake their heads and say the three will not live or reach Dawson.

s.t: Buck was very weak, but he did not stop.
s.fr: Buck était à bout de forces, mais il ne s’arrêtait pas.

s.t: He pulled the sled with the three other dogs, and he lay in the snow at night.
s.fr: Il tirait le traîneau avec les trois autres chiens et, la nuit, s’affalait dans la neige.

s.t: He did not dig a hole, for he could not stand.
s.fr: Il ne creusait même plus de trou, car il ne tenait plus debout.

s.t: The wind was cold, and the snow came down.
s.fr: Le vent était glacé, et la neige tombait.

paras.summary: Buck is very weak but does not stop, pulling the sled with three other dogs and lying in the snow at night because he cannot stand to dig.

s.t: The days grew longer, and the sun was warm on the snow.
s.fr: Les jours rallongèrent, et le soleil chauffait la neige.

s.t: The snow was soft, and the ice on the river was thin.
s.fr: La neige se ramollit, et la glace de la rivière s’amincit.

s.t: The trail was wet, and the sled was hard to pull.
s.fr: La piste était détrempée, et le traîneau devenait pénible à tirer.

s.t: Buck did not know what the soft snow meant.
s.fr: Buck ignorait ce que présageait cette neige molle.

paras.summary: The days grow longer and the sun warm, the snow turns soft and the river ice thin, and Buck does not know what it means.

s.t: At last the sled came to a camp by the river, and a man named John Thornton stood by the fire.
s.fr: Enfin, le traîneau atteignit un campement au bord de la rivière, où un homme nommé John Thornton se tenait près du feu.

s.t: He looked at the thin dogs, and then he looked at Hal.
s.fr: Il regarda les chiens efflanqués, puis Hal.

s.t: "Do not go on the ice," Thornton said, "for the ice is thin, and it will break."
s.fr: « Ne vous aventurez pas sur la glace, dit Thornton, elle est mince et elle va céder. »

s.t: "Other men told us to stay," Hal said, "but we will go on."
s.fr: « D’autres nous ont déjà dit de rester, répondit Hal, mais nous continuerons. »

paras.summary: The sled comes to a river camp where John Thornton warns Hal that the ice is thin and will break, but Hal says they will go on.

s.t: "The ice will not hold you," Thornton said.
s.fr: « La glace ne vous portera pas, » dit Thornton.

s.t: "I will not stay here," Hal said, "for we are going to Dawson."
s.fr: « Je ne resterai pas ici, dit Hal, nous allons à Dawson. »

s.t: Hal took his whip, and he hit the dogs.
s.fr: Hal prit son fouet et frappa les chiens.

s.t: The dogs stood up, but Buck lay in the snow and did not move.
s.fr: Les chiens se levèrent, mais Buck resta couché dans la neige, sans bouger.

paras.summary: Thornton says the ice will not hold them, but Hal says they are going to Dawson and whips the dogs, and all stand except Buck, who lies still.

s.t: Buck knew that the ice was thin, and he felt that danger was near.
s.fr: Buck savait que la glace était mince, et il flairait le danger tout proche.

s.t: He did not want to go on the ice, and he was very tired.
s.fr: Il ne voulait pas s’engager sur la glace, et il était à bout de forces.

s.t: Hal hit Buck again and again, but Buck did not get up.
s.fr: Hal roua Buck de coups, mais Buck ne se leva pas.

s.t: "Get up!" Hal shouted.
s.fr: « Debout ! » cria Hal.

s.t: "Get up, or I will kill you!"
s.fr: « Debout, ou je te tue ! »

paras.summary: Buck knows that the ice is thin and does not want to go on it, and Hal hits him again and again and shouts at him to get up.

s.t: Thornton stood up and looked at Hal.
s.fr: Thornton se leva et toisa Hal.

s.t: "If you hit that dog again," he said, "I will kill you."
s.fr: « Si vous frappez encore ce chien, dit-il, je vous tue. »

s.t: "That is not your dog," Hal said.
s.fr: « Ce n’est pas votre chien, » dit Hal.

s.t: "He is not your dog now," Thornton said, and he took out his knife.
s.fr: « Ce n’est plus le vôtre, » répliqua Thornton en sortant son couteau.

paras.summary: Thornton says he will kill Hal if he hits the dog again, and takes out his knife.

s.t: Thornton cut the ropes of the harness, and Buck was free.
s.fr: Thornton trancha les traits du harnais, et Buck fut libre.

s.t: Hal laughed, and he shouted at the other dogs, and the sled went out on the ice.
s.fr: Hal ricana, cria après les autres chiens, et le traîneau s’engagea sur la glace.

s.t: Thornton and Buck watched from the shore, and no one spoke.
s.fr: Depuis la rive, Thornton et Buck regardaient en silence.

s.t: The sled went a little way, and then the ice broke.
s.fr: Le traîneau alla un peu plus loin, puis la glace céda.

paras.summary: Thornton cuts Buck's ropes, Hal laughs and drives the sled out on the ice, and Thornton and Buck watch from the shore until the ice breaks.

s.t: The sled fell into the river, and Hal and Charles and Mercedes fell with it.
s.fr: Le traîneau s’abîma dans la rivière, entraînant Hal, Charles et Mercedes.

s.t: The dogs fell too, and in a moment they were all gone.
s.fr: Les chiens suivirent, et en un instant tous avaient disparu.

s.t: Nothing was left on the ice but a great hole.
s.fr: Il ne resta sur la glace qu’un grand trou béant.

s.t: "You poor dog," Thornton said, and he put his hand on Buck's head.
s.fr: « Mon pauvre chien, » dit Thornton en posant la main sur la tête de Buck.

s.t: Buck lay at his feet and looked up at his face.
s.fr: Buck s’allongea à ses pieds et leva les yeux vers son visage.

paras.summary: The sled falls into the river with Hal, Charles, Mercedes and the dogs, leaving only a great hole, and Thornton puts his hand on Buck's head.

chapterList.title: For the Love of a Man

s.t: Thornton took Buck to his camp and let him rest by the fire.
s.fr: Thornton emmena Buck à son campement et le laissa se reposer près du feu.

s.t: Buck ate meat and slept for many days, and his strength came back.
s.fr: Buck mangea de la viande et dormit des jours entiers, et ses forces lui revinrent.

s.t: Thornton had two partners, Hans and Pete, and they lived in the camp with him.
s.fr: Thornton avait deux associés, Hans et Pete, qui partageaient son campement.

s.t: They also had two dogs, a little dog named Skeet and a big black dog named Nig.
s.fr: Ils avaient aussi deux chiens : une petite chienne nommée Skeet et un grand chien noir nommé Nig.

paras.summary: Thornton takes Buck to his camp to rest by the fire, and Buck eats, sleeps and grows strong again, living with Thornton's partners Hans and Pete and their dogs Skeet and Nig.

s.t: Skeet came to Buck and licked his wounds, and Buck let her.
s.fr: Skeet vint lécher les blessures de Buck, qui la laissa faire.

s.t: Nig was friendly too, and he played with Buck in the snow.
s.fr: Nig, tout aussi aimable, jouait avec Buck dans la neige.

s.t: Buck was not afraid of these dogs, and he did not want to fight them.
s.fr: Buck ne craignait pas ces chiens et n’avait aucune envie de se battre avec eux.

s.t: He knew that he was safe in this camp.
s.fr: Il savait que dans ce campement, il ne risquait rien.

paras.summary: Skeet licks Buck's wounds and Nig plays with him, and Buck does not want to fight them and knows he is safe.

s.t: Thornton took Buck's head in his hands and shook it gently.
s.fr: Thornton prit la tête de Buck entre ses mains et la secoua doucement.

s.t: "You are a good dog, Buck," he said, "and I am glad that I found you."
s.fr: « Tu es un bon chien, Buck, dit-il, et je suis content de t’avoir trouvé. »

s.t: "You are a very good dog," he said again, "and you will stay with me."
s.fr: « Tu es un très bon chien, répéta-t-il, et tu vas rester avec moi. »

s.t: Buck did not know the words, but he knew that Thornton was his friend.
s.fr: Buck ne comprenait pas les mots, mais il savait que Thornton était son ami.

paras.summary: Thornton takes Buck's head in his hands and tells him he is a good dog and will stay, and Buck knows he is a friend.

s.t: "He is the best dog I have seen," Thornton said to Hans and Pete.
s.fr: « C’est le meilleur chien que j’aie jamais vu, » dit Thornton à Hans et à Pete.

s.t: "He is very big," Hans said, "and he is strong."
s.fr: « Il est très grand, dit Hans, et fort, avec ça. »

s.t: "He will be a good dog for the sled," Pete said.
s.fr: « Il fera un bon chien de traîneau, » dit Pete.

s.t: "He will stay with me," Thornton said, "and he will not go with any other man."
s.fr: « Il restera avec moi, dit Thornton, et il ne suivra personne d’autre. »

paras.summary: Thornton tells Hans and Pete that Buck is the best dog he has seen, and they agree he is big and strong, and Thornton says Buck will stay with him.

s.t: Buck had loved Judge Miller, but this was a greater love.
s.fr: Buck avait aimé le juge Miller, mais il connaissait à présent un amour plus grand encore.

s.t: Thornton had saved his life, and he was the best master Buck had ever known.
s.fr: Thornton lui avait sauvé la vie, et c’était le meilleur maître que Buck eût jamais connu.

s.t: Buck lay at his feet all day and watched his face.
s.fr: Buck passait ses journées couché à ses pieds, les yeux fixés sur son visage.

s.t: When Thornton went away, Buck followed him, and when he came back, Buck was there.
s.fr: Quand Thornton s’éloignait, Buck le suivait, et quand il revenait, Buck était là.

paras.summary: Buck loves Thornton more than he loved Judge Miller, because Thornton saved his life, and watches him and follows him everywhere.

s.t: Buck did not leave the camp, for he did not want to lose his master.
s.fr: Buck ne quittait pas le campement, de peur de perdre son maître.

s.t: He remembered Perrault and Francois, and he remembered the mail man.
s.fr: Il se souvenait de Perrault et de François, et aussi de l’homme du courrier.

s.t: But Thornton was different, and Buck was afraid that Thornton would go away.
s.fr: Mais Thornton n’était pas comme eux, et Buck craignait qu’il ne s’en aille à son tour.

s.t: At night Buck lay by the fire, and he did not dream of the hairy man.
s.fr: La nuit, Buck se couchait près du feu, et il ne rêvait plus de l’homme velu.

paras.summary: Buck does not leave the camp because he fears losing his master, remembers his old masters, and no longer dreams of the hairy man.

s.t: In the spring Thornton and his partners went to Dawson, and Buck went with them.
s.fr: Au printemps, Thornton et ses associés se rendirent à Dawson, et Buck les accompagna.

s.t: One night Thornton sat in a house where many men drank and talked, and Buck lay at his feet.
s.fr: Un soir, Thornton était assis dans une taverne pleine d’hommes qui buvaient et bavardaient, Buck couché à ses pieds.

s.t: A man named Burton stood near the fire, and he was angry with another man.
s.fr: Un homme nommé Burton se tenait près du feu, en colère contre un autre homme.

s.t: "You are a fool," Burton said, and he hit the other man in the face.
s.fr: « Tu es un imbécile, » dit Burton, et il frappa l’autre au visage.

paras.summary: In the spring Thornton and his partners go to Dawson with Buck, and one night Burton, an angry man in a house full of men, hits another man in the face.

s.t: Thornton stood up and said that Burton must stop.
s.fr: Thornton se leva et dit à Burton d’arrêter.

s.t: "You must not hit him," Thornton said.
s.fr: « Ne le frappez pas, » dit Thornton.

s.t: Burton turned and hit Thornton, and Thornton fell down on the floor.
s.fr: Burton se retourna et frappa Thornton, qui s’écroula sur le plancher.

s.t: The men shouted, and no one moved, for they were afraid of Burton.
s.fr: Les hommes crièrent, mais personne ne bougea, car tous craignaient Burton.

paras.summary: Thornton tells Burton to stop, but Burton hits him and Thornton falls, and the men are afraid to move.

s.t: Buck saw his master on the floor, and he jumped at Burton's throat.
s.fr: Buck vit son maître à terre et sauta à la gorge de Burton.

s.t: Burton put up his arm, but Buck's teeth were in it, and blood came.
s.fr: Burton leva le bras, mais les crocs de Buck s’y enfoncèrent, et le sang jaillit.

s.t: Buck jumped again, and this time he bit Burton's neck.
s.fr: Buck bondit de nouveau, et cette fois il mordit Burton au cou.

s.t: The men pulled Buck away, and Burton fell down on the floor.
s.fr: Les hommes tirèrent Buck en arrière, et Burton s’effondra sur le plancher.

paras.summary: Buck jumps at Burton's throat, bites his arm and neck, and the men pull Buck away.

s.t: A doctor came and looked at Burton, and Burton lived.
s.fr: Un médecin vint examiner Burton, qui survécut.

s.t: The men talked about Buck all that night, and they were not angry with him.
s.fr: Les hommes parlèrent de Buck toute la nuit, sans lui en vouloir le moins du monde.

s.t: "That dog did right," they said, "for he saved his master."
s.fr: « Ce chien a eu raison, disaient-ils, il a sauvé son maître. »

s.t: Everyone in Dawson knew about Buck after that night.
s.fr: Après cette nuit-là, tout Dawson connaissait Buck.

paras.summary: A doctor sees Burton, who lives, and the men say that Buck did right to save his master, and everyone in Dawson knows about Buck.

s.t: In the summer Thornton and his partners took a boat down a fast river.
s.fr: L’été venu, Thornton et ses associés descendirent en barque une rivière rapide.

s.t: Hans and Pete stood on the bank with a rope, and Thornton stood in the boat with a pole.
s.fr: Hans et Pete tenaient une corde depuis la berge, tandis que Thornton, debout dans la barque, maniait une perche.

s.t: Buck ran along the bank, and he watched Thornton all the time.
s.fr: Buck courait le long de la berge, sans quitter Thornton des yeux.

s.t: The river was fast, and the water went over the rocks with a great noise.
s.fr: Le courant était rapide, et l’eau se ruait sur les rochers dans un grand fracas.

paras.summary: In the summer the three men take a boat down a fast river, with Hans and Pete holding a rope from the bank, Thornton in the boat with a pole, and Buck running along the bank.

s.t: The boat turned in the water, and Thornton fell out of it.
s.fr: La barque pivota dans le courant, et Thornton passa par-dessus bord.

s.t: The river took him, and he could not stand up.
s.fr: Le courant l’emporta, et il ne put reprendre pied.

s.t: Buck did not wait, and he jumped into the river and swam to his master.
s.fr: Buck n’attendit pas : il sauta dans la rivière et nagea vers son maître.

s.t: Thornton took Buck by the neck, and Buck swam to the bank with him.
s.fr: Thornton agrippa Buck par le cou, et Buck nagea vers la berge en le remorquant.

paras.summary: The boat turns and Thornton falls into the fast river, and Buck jumps in and swims to him, and Thornton takes Buck by the neck as he swims to the bank.

s.t: Hans and Pete pulled the rope, and they pulled Thornton and Buck to the bank.
s.fr: Hans et Pete halèrent la corde et ramenèrent Thornton et Buck jusqu’à la berge.

s.t: Thornton lay on the ground, and he could not speak for a long time.
s.fr: Thornton resta étendu sur le sol, longtemps incapable de parler.

s.t: Buck lay beside him and put his head on Thornton's hand.
s.fr: Buck se coucha à côté de lui et posa la tête sur sa main.

s.t: "You are a good dog, Buck," Thornton said at last.
s.fr: « Tu es un bon chien, Buck, » dit enfin Thornton.

s.t: "You saved my life, and I will not forget it."
s.fr: « Tu m’as sauvé la vie, et je ne l’oublierai pas. »

paras.summary: Hans and Pete pull them to the bank, and Thornton lies unable to speak until he tells Buck he is a good dog who saved his life.

s.t: Thornton and his partners needed money, for they wanted to go far into the north to look for gold.
s.fr: Thornton et ses associés avaient besoin d’argent, car ils voulaient s’enfoncer loin dans le Nord à la recherche d’or.

s.t: One day in Dawson a man named Matthewson talked about his dog.
s.fr: Un jour, à Dawson, un homme nommé Matthewson vantait les mérites de son chien.

s.t: "My dog can pull a sled with 1000 pounds on it," Matthewson said.
s.fr: « Mon chien peut tirer un traîneau chargé de mille livres, » affirma Matthewson.

s.t: "Buck can pull it too," Thornton said.
s.fr: « Buck peut en faire autant, » dit Thornton.

paras.summary: Thornton and his partners need money to look for gold, and in Dawson Matthewson says his dog can pull a sled with 1000 pounds, and Thornton says Buck can too.

s.t: "Can Buck start a sled with 1000 pounds on it?" Matthewson asked.
s.fr: « Buck peut-il arracher un traîneau chargé de mille livres ? » demanda Matthewson.

s.t: "Can he walk 100 yards with it?"
s.fr: « Et le traîner sur cent yards ? »

s.t: "He can," Thornton said.
s.fr: « Il le peut, » dit Thornton.

s.t: "Then I will bet you 1000 dollars that he cannot," Matthewson said.
s.fr: « Alors je vous parie mille dollars qu’il n’y arrivera pas, » dit Matthewson.

s.t: Thornton did not have 1000 dollars, and he did not know what to say.
s.fr: Thornton n’avait pas mille dollars, et il ne sut que répondre.

paras.summary: Matthewson asks if Buck can start the sled and walk 100 yards and bets 1000 dollars that he cannot, but Thornton does not have the money.

s.t: Thornton asked a friend, and the friend gave him the money.
s.fr: Thornton s’adressa à un ami, qui lui avança la somme.

s.t: Many men came to see the sled, and they bet on the other dog.
s.fr: Beaucoup d’hommes vinrent voir le traîneau, et ils misèrent sur l’autre chien.

s.t: The sled was heavy, and the ice held it to the ground.
s.fr: Le traîneau était lourd, et la glace le soudait au sol.

s.t: "That dog cannot move it," a man said.
s.fr: « Ce chien ne le bougera jamais, » dit un homme.

s.t: "He can," said another man.
s.fr: « Mais si, il le peut, » dit un autre.

paras.summary: A friend lends Thornton the money, and many men come to see the heavy sled held by the ice, and some say the dog cannot move it and some say he can.

s.t: Thornton stood beside Buck and took his head in his hands.
s.fr: Thornton se plaça à côté de Buck et lui prit la tête entre ses mains.

s.t: "Do it for me, Buck," he said.
s.fr: « Fais-le pour moi, Buck, » dit-il.

s.t: "Do it for me."
s.fr: « Fais-le pour moi. »

s.t: Buck licked his hand and looked at his master's face.
s.fr: Buck lui lécha la main et leva les yeux vers le visage de son maître.

s.t: Then he stood up and went to the sled.
s.fr: Puis il se leva et alla se placer devant le traîneau.

paras.summary: Thornton stands beside Buck and asks him to do it for him, and Buck licks his hand and goes to the sled.

s.t: "Now, Buck," Thornton shouted.
s.fr: « Allez, Buck ! » cria Thornton.

s.t: "Pull!"
s.fr: « Tire ! »

s.t: Buck pulled as hard as he could, and the sled moved a little.
s.fr: Buck tira de toutes ses forces, et le traîneau bougea légèrement.

s.t: The ice under the sled broke, and the sled began to move.
s.fr: La glace céda sous le traîneau, qui se mit en marche.

s.t: Buck pulled again, and he pulled the sled along the street.
s.fr: Buck tira de nouveau et entraîna le traîneau le long de la rue.

paras.summary: Thornton shouts for Buck to pull, and the sled moves, the ice under it breaks, and Buck pulls it along the street.

s.t: Buck pulled the sled for 100 yards, and there he stopped.
s.fr: Buck tira le traîneau sur cent yards, et là, il s’arrêta.

s.t: The men shouted, and some of them cried.
s.fr: Une clameur s’éleva, et certains hommes pleuraient.

s.t: Thornton put his arms around Buck and held him.
s.fr: Thornton jeta les bras autour du cou de Buck et le serra contre lui.

s.t: He had won 1000 dollars, and Buck had won it for him.
s.fr: Il avait gagné mille dollars, et c’était Buck qui les lui avait gagnés.

s.t: Thornton paid his friend the money, and then he and his partners had money for the long trip.
s.fr: Thornton rendit l’argent à son ami, et ses associés et lui eurent de quoi payer le long voyage.

s.t: That night he gave Buck the best meat in all of Dawson.
s.fr: Ce soir-là, il offrit à Buck la meilleure viande de tout Dawson.

paras.summary: Buck pulls the sled 100 yards and stops, the men shout and some cry, and Thornton holds Buck, having won the money.

s.t: Thornton and his partners wanted to find a lost cabin in the east, and men said that there was much gold near it.
s.fr: Thornton et ses associés voulaient retrouver une cabane perdue dans l’Est, près de laquelle, disait-on, l’or abondait.

s.t: No man had found the cabin, but many men had looked for it.
s.fr: Personne n’avait jamais trouvé la cabane, mais beaucoup l’avaient cherchée.

s.t: Thornton took Pete and Hans, and they went east with Buck and six other dogs.
s.fr: Thornton emmena Pete et Hans, et ils partirent vers l’Est avec Buck et six autres chiens.

s.t: They had food for many days, and they were not afraid.
s.fr: Ils emportaient des vivres pour bien des jours et ne craignaient rien.

paras.summary: Thornton, Pete and Hans go east with Buck and six other dogs to find a lost cabin with gold near it, taking food for many days.

s.t: They went through forests and over rivers, and they did not stop.
s.fr: Ils traversèrent des forêts, franchirent des rivières, sans jamais s’arrêter.

s.t: When they had no food, they killed animals, and they ate fish from the water.
s.fr: Quand les vivres venaient à manquer, ils tuaient du gibier et pêchaient du poisson.

s.t: The days were long, and the nights were short, for it was summer.
s.fr: Les jours étaient longs et les nuits courtes, car c’était l’été.
