s.t: Buck pulled the sled, and he was strong and glad.
s.fr: Buck tirait le traîneau, plein de force et de joie.

paras.summary: They travel through forests and over rivers, killing animals and catching fish when the food is gone, in the long days of summer, and Buck pulls the sled, strong and glad.

s.t: At last they came to a wide valley, and there was gold in the ground.
s.fr: Enfin, ils arrivèrent dans une large vallée où la terre recelait de l’or.

s.t: The men washed the gold out of the ground in a river, and they worked from morning until night.
s.fr: Les hommes lavaient la terre dans la rivière pour en extraire l’or, et ils travaillaient du matin au soir.

s.t: Each man had a pan, and he shook it in the water until the gold lay at the bottom.
s.fr: Chacun avait sa batée, qu’il secouait dans l’eau jusqu’à ce que l’or se dépose au fond.

s.t: The men filled small bags with the gold, and each day they had more.
s.fr: Les hommes remplissaient d’or de petits sacs, et chaque jour ils en avaient davantage.

s.t: They did not find the lost cabin, but they did not need it.
s.fr: Ils ne trouvèrent pas la cabane perdue, mais ils n’en avaient plus besoin.

s.t: "We are rich," Pete said, "and we will not be poor again."
s.fr: « Nous sommes riches, dit Pete, et nous ne serons plus jamais pauvres. »

paras.summary: They reach a wide valley with gold in the ground, fill bags with gold each day, and Pete says they are rich and will not be poor again.

s.t: At night the men sat by the fire and talked about the gold.
s.fr: Le soir, les hommes s’asseyaient autour du feu et parlaient de l’or.

s.t: "What will you do with the gold?" Hans asked.
s.fr: « Que feras-tu de ton or ? » demanda Hans.

s.t: "I will buy a farm," Pete said.
s.fr: « Je m’achèterai une ferme, » dit Pete.

s.t: "I will buy a boat," Hans said, "and I will go home."
s.fr: « Moi, je m’achèterai un bateau, dit Hans, et je rentrerai au pays. »

s.t: "I will stay here with Buck," Thornton said, "for I do not want to go home."
s.fr: « Moi, je resterai ici avec Buck, dit Thornton, car je n’ai aucune envie de rentrer. »

paras.summary: At night the men talk about what they will do with the gold, Pete a farm, Hans a boat, and Thornton says he will stay with Buck.

s.t: The men worked all day, and Buck had nothing to do.
s.fr: Les hommes travaillaient toute la journée, et Buck n’avait rien à faire.

s.t: He lay by the fire and watched the men, and he thought about the wild dogs.
s.fr: Il restait couché près du feu à regarder les hommes, et il songeait aux chiens sauvages.

s.t: At night he dreamed again of the hairy man, and the dream was clearer.
s.fr: La nuit, il rêva de nouveau de l’homme velu, et le rêve était plus net.

s.t: He heard a sound in the forest, and it was the sound of a call.
s.fr: Il entendit dans la forêt un son, et ce son était un appel.

paras.summary: While the men work, Buck lies by the fire thinking about wild dogs, dreams again of the hairy man, and hears a sound like a call in the forest.

s.t: After that night Buck heard the cry in the forest every night, and each time it was clearer.
s.fr: Après cette nuit-là, Buck entendit chaque nuit le hurlement dans la forêt, et chaque fois plus net.

s.t: It was a long cry, and it was not the cry of a dog.
s.fr: C’était un long hurlement, et ce n’était pas celui d’un chien.

s.t: One night Buck got up from the fire and walked into the trees.
s.fr: Une nuit, Buck quitta le feu et s’enfonça sous les arbres.

s.t: Thornton was asleep, and no man saw Buck go.
s.fr: Thornton dormait, et personne ne vit Buck partir.

paras.summary: Every night Buck hears a cry in the forest that is not the cry of a dog, and one night he leaves the sleeping camp and walks into the trees.

s.t: Buck went a long way through the forest, and he came to an open place among the trees.
s.fr: Buck parcourut un long chemin à travers la forêt et déboucha dans une clairière.

s.t: A wolf sat there with his nose in the air, and he was thin and grey.
s.fr: Un loup y était assis, le museau en l’air, maigre et gris.

s.t: Buck came near him slowly, and he moved his tail to show that he was a friend.
s.fr: Buck s’approcha de lui lentement, en remuant la queue pour montrer qu’il venait en ami.

s.t: The wolf did not want a friend, and he ran away.
s.fr: Le loup ne voulait pas d’ami, et il s’enfuit.

s.t: Buck ran after him, and the wolf turned and showed his teeth.
s.fr: Buck le poursuivit, et le loup fit volte-face en montrant les crocs.

paras.summary: In an open place Buck finds a thin grey wolf, who runs away and then turns to show his teeth.

s.t: Buck stopped and did not growl, and he held his nose out to the wolf.
s.fr: Buck s’arrêta sans gronder et tendit le museau vers le loup.

s.t: The wolf looked at him for a moment, and then the two of them touched noses.
s.fr: Le loup le considéra un moment, puis ils se touchèrent le museau.

s.t: After that the wolf was friendly, and he ran on ahead through the trees.
s.fr: Dès lors, le loup se radoucit, et il s’élança en avant à travers les arbres.

s.t: Buck ran beside the wolf, and the two of them went a long way in the night.
s.fr: Buck courait aux côtés du loup, et tous deux firent un long chemin dans la nuit.

s.t: They came to a stream, and both of them drank from it.
s.fr: Ils arrivèrent à un ruisseau, où ils burent tous deux.

paras.summary: Buck holds out his nose, the wolf touches noses with him, and the two run together to a stream and drink.

s.t: The wolf looked back at Buck and cried, and he wanted Buck to come with him.
s.fr: Le loup se retourna vers Buck et gémit : il voulait que Buck le suive.

s.t: Buck knew that the wolf was like him, and he was glad to have a friend in the forest.
s.fr: Buck sentait que le loup était son semblable, et il était heureux d’avoir un ami dans la forêt.

s.t: But he thought of Thornton, and he stopped.
s.fr: Mais il pensa à Thornton, et il s’arrêta.

s.t: The wolf cried again, and Buck turned back toward the camp.
s.fr: Le loup gémit de nouveau, et Buck rebroussa chemin vers le campement.

s.t: The wolf ran beside him for a while, and then he sat down on the ground and cried at the sky.
s.fr: Le loup courut à ses côtés un moment, puis il s’assit par terre et hurla vers le ciel.

s.t: Buck ran on and did not look back, but he heard the cry behind him for a long time.
s.fr: Buck poursuivit sa course sans se retourner, mais il entendit longtemps le hurlement derrière lui.

paras.summary: The wolf wants Buck to come farther, but Buck thinks of Thornton and turns back while the wolf cries behind him.

s.t: When he came to the camp, Thornton was awake, and he stood by the fire.
s.fr: Quand il regagna le campement, Thornton était réveillé, debout près du feu.

s.t: Buck jumped on him and licked his face, and Thornton laughed and shook him.
s.fr: Buck lui sauta dessus et lui lécha le visage, et Thornton le secoua en riant.

s.t: "You are a fool dog, Buck," Thornton said.
s.fr: « Tu n’es qu’un grand nigaud de chien, Buck, » dit Thornton.

s.t: Buck did not know the words, but he knew that Thornton was glad to see him.
s.fr: Buck ne comprenait pas les mots, mais il savait que Thornton était heureux de le revoir.

paras.summary: Buck comes to the camp, where Thornton is awake, jumps on him and licks his face, and Thornton laughs at him.

s.t: For two days Buck stayed in the camp and did not leave Thornton.
s.fr: Pendant deux jours, Buck resta au campement sans quitter Thornton.

s.t: But that night the cry came again, and Buck could not lie by the fire.
s.fr: Mais cette nuit-là, le hurlement retentit de nouveau, et Buck ne put rester couché près du feu.

s.t: He went into the forest and looked for the wolf, but he did not find him.
s.fr: Il s’enfonça dans la forêt à la recherche du loup, mais ne le trouva pas.

s.t: Buck slept among the trees, and in the morning he was hungry.
s.fr: Buck dormit sous les arbres, et au matin il avait faim.

s.t: Thornton had always given him food, and now he must find his own.
s.fr: C’était toujours Thornton qui l’avait nourri ; désormais, il lui fallait se débrouiller seul.

paras.summary: Buck stays two days with Thornton, then goes into the forest when the cry comes again, and finds he must look for his own food.

s.t: He stood still in a stream for a long time, and at last a fish came near.
s.fr: Il resta longtemps sans bouger dans un ruisseau, et enfin un poisson passa à sa portée.

s.t: Buck caught the fish in his mouth, and he ate it.
s.fr: Buck happa le poisson et le dévora.

s.t: The next day he caught a rabbit, and the day after that he caught another.
s.fr: Le lendemain, il attrapa un lièvre, et le surlendemain un autre.

s.t: Buck learned to wait for a long time, and he learned to walk without a sound.
s.fr: Buck apprit à attendre longtemps et à se déplacer sans un bruit.

s.t: He learned to hunt as the wolves hunted, and he was not afraid in the forest.
s.fr: Il apprit à chasser à la manière des loups, et la forêt ne lui faisait plus peur.

paras.summary: Buck catches fish and rabbits and learns to hunt as the wolves do, without a sound and without fear.

s.t: Each time he wanted to see Thornton, he went back to the camp and lay by the fire.
s.fr: Chaque fois qu’il avait envie de voir Thornton, il revenait au campement et se couchait près du feu.

s.t: "Where did you go, Buck?" Thornton asked.
s.fr: « Où étais-tu passé, Buck ? » demandait Thornton.

s.t: "Do you love the forest more than you love me?"
s.fr: « Tu aimes donc la forêt plus que moi ? »

s.t: Buck put his head on Thornton's knee, and Thornton laughed.
s.fr: Buck posait la tête sur le genou de Thornton, qui riait.

paras.summary: Buck returns to the camp whenever he wants to see Thornton, and Thornton asks where he went.

s.t: In the fall Hans and Pete took their gold, and they went home down the river.
s.fr: À l’automne, Hans et Pete prirent leur or et redescendirent la rivière pour rentrer chez eux.

s.t: "Come with us, John," Hans said.
s.fr: « Viens avec nous, John, » dit Hans.

s.t: "I will stay here with Buck," Thornton said, "for there is more gold in this valley."
s.fr: « Je reste ici avec Buck, dit Thornton, il y a encore de l’or dans cette vallée. »

s.t: Hans and Pete went away, and Thornton was left in the camp with Buck and Nig.
s.fr: Hans et Pete partirent, et Thornton resta seul au campement avec Buck et Nig.

paras.summary: In the fall Hans and Pete go home with their gold, and Thornton stays in the valley with Buck and Nig.

s.t: Every night Thornton talked to Buck by the fire, and Buck lay still and looked at his face.
s.fr: Chaque soir, au coin du feu, Thornton parlait à Buck, qui l’écoutait sans bouger, les yeux levés vers son visage.

s.t: Buck loved Thornton, and he stayed near him through the days.
s.fr: Buck aimait Thornton et ne s’éloignait pas de lui de la journée.

s.t: But each night the cry came from the forest, and each night Buck wanted to go.
s.fr: Mais chaque nuit, le hurlement montait de la forêt, et chaque nuit Buck brûlait de partir.

s.t: Buck went to the trees, and each time he stayed away longer.
s.fr: Buck partait sous les arbres, et chaque fois son absence durait plus longtemps.

s.t: Thornton waited for him by the fire, and each time Buck came back.
s.fr: Thornton l’attendait près du feu, et chaque fois Buck revenait.

paras.summary: Thornton talks to Buck each night by the fire, and Buck loves him, but the cry from the forest grows harder to refuse, and each time he stays away longer.

s.t: Soon the first snow came, and a herd of moose came down from the hills.
s.fr: Bientôt tomba la première neige, et une harde d’élans descendit des collines.

s.t: Buck stood among the trees and watched them.
s.fr: Posté sous les arbres, Buck les guettait.

s.t: In the middle of the herd there was a bull, and he had wide antlers.
s.fr: Au milieu de la harde se trouvait un mâle aux larges bois.

s.t: The bull was taller than Buck, and he was old, and he was strong.
s.fr: Le mâle était plus grand que Buck, vieux et puissant.

s.t: Buck wanted to kill him, and he went after the herd.
s.fr: Buck voulait le tuer, et il se lança sur les traces de la harde.

paras.summary: The first snow comes, a herd of moose comes down from the hills, and Buck sees an old bull with wide antlers and goes after him.

s.t: The bull turned and looked at Buck, and his eyes were angry.
s.fr: Le mâle se retourna et fixa Buck d’un œil chargé de colère.

s.t: Buck ran at the herd again and again, and each time the bull came to meet him with his antlers.
s.fr: Buck chargea la harde encore et encore, et chaque fois le mâle lui faisait face, les bois baissés.

s.t: Buck could not get past the bull, but he did not stop.
s.fr: Buck ne parvenait pas à déborder le mâle, mais il ne renonçait pas.

s.t: At last the herd moved on, for the other moose did not want to wait, and the old bull was left alone with Buck.
s.fr: Enfin la harde reprit sa route, car les autres élans ne voulaient pas attendre, et le vieux mâle resta seul face à Buck.

paras.summary: The bull meets Buck's attacks with his antlers, until the herd moves on and leaves the old bull alone with Buck.

s.t: For four days and four nights Buck stayed near the bull and did not let him rest.
s.fr: Pendant quatre jours et quatre nuits, Buck ne lâcha pas le mâle et ne lui laissa aucun répit.

s.t: The bull could not eat, and he could not sleep, and he could not drink at the streams.
s.fr: Le mâle ne pouvait ni manger, ni dormir, ni boire aux ruisseaux.

s.t: Every time he stopped, Buck ran at him, and the bull went on with his head down.
s.fr: Chaque fois qu’il s’arrêtait, Buck fonçait sur lui, et le mâle repartait, tête basse.

s.t: Buck did not get tired, for he had grown strong in the forest.
s.fr: Buck ne se lassait pas, car la forêt l’avait endurci.

s.t: The bull grew weaker every hour, and Buck knew that the end was near.
s.fr: Le mâle faiblissait d’heure en heure, et Buck savait que la fin était proche.

paras.summary: For four days Buck stays near the bull and does not let him eat, sleep or drink, and the bull grows weaker every hour.

s.t: On the fourth day the bull stopped and stood still with his head down.
s.fr: Le quatrième jour, le mâle s’arrêta et resta planté là, la tête basse.

s.t: He was too weak to run, and he did not lift his antlers when Buck came.
s.fr: Trop faible pour fuir, il ne releva même pas ses bois à l’approche de Buck.

s.t: Buck jumped at his throat, and the bull fell down on the ground and died.
s.fr: Buck lui sauta à la gorge, et le mâle s’effondra et mourut.

s.t: Buck ate the meat, and he slept beside the bull for a day and a night.
s.fr: Buck se reput de sa chair et dormit un jour et une nuit auprès de sa proie.

paras.summary: On the fourth day the bull is too weak to lift his antlers, Buck kills him, and Buck eats and sleeps beside the meat.

s.t: When he woke, he thought of Thornton, and he wanted to go back to the camp.
s.fr: À son réveil, il pensa à Thornton et voulut regagner le campement.

s.t: He smelled something in the wind, and it was the smell of men, but not the smell of Thornton.
s.fr: Il flaira quelque chose dans le vent : une odeur d’hommes, mais pas celle de Thornton.

s.t: Buck did not know why, but he knew that something was wrong.
s.fr: Buck n’aurait su dire pourquoi, mais il savait que quelque chose n’allait pas.

s.t: He got up and ran toward the camp.
s.fr: Il se leva et fila vers le campement.

paras.summary: Buck wakes thinking of Thornton, smells men who are not Thornton on the wind, and runs toward the camp.

s.t: Buck ran through the forest all that day, and he did not stop to rest.
s.fr: Buck courut à travers la forêt toute la journée, sans prendre le temps de se reposer.

s.t: Near the camp he came to a trail, and Nig lay dead on it.
s.fr: Près du campement, il tomba sur une piste où gisait le cadavre de Nig.

s.t: There was an arrow in Nig's side, and Buck knew that men had done it.
s.fr: Une flèche était plantée dans son flanc, et Buck comprit que c’était l’œuvre des hommes.

s.t: He went on slowly and came to the edge of the camp.
s.fr: Il avança lentement jusqu’à la lisière du campement.

paras.summary: Buck runs through the forest to the camp and finds Nig dead on the trail with an arrow in his side.

s.t: Thornton's tent was torn, and his things lay on the ground.
s.fr: La tente de Thornton était déchirée, et ses affaires jonchaient le sol.

s.t: Many men were dancing around the tent, and Buck had never seen them before.
s.fr: Une foule d’hommes que Buck n’avait jamais vus dansaient autour de la tente.

s.t: They were Yeehats, and they had come to the camp while Buck was in the forest.
s.fr: C’étaient des Yeehats, venus au campement pendant que Buck courait la forêt.

s.t: The Yeehats shouted and laughed, and they did not see Buck in the trees.
s.fr: Les Yeehats criaient et riaient, sans voir Buck caché parmi les arbres.

s.t: Buck heard a roar, and it was his own voice.
s.fr: Buck entendit un rugissement : c’était sa propre voix.

paras.summary: Buck sees Thornton's tent torn and strange men dancing around it, and he hears a roar that is his own voice.

s.t: He ran at the men with all his strength, and he jumped at the first of them.
s.fr: Il fondit sur les hommes de toutes ses forces et se jeta sur le premier d’entre eux.

s.t: That man was the chief of the Yeehats, and Buck cut open his throat.
s.fr: Cet homme était le chef des Yeehats, et Buck lui ouvrit la gorge.

s.t: The chief fell down on the ground, and his blood ran out.
s.fr: Le chef s’effondra, et son sang se répandit sur le sol.

s.t: Buck did not stop, and he jumped at the next man and killed him too.
s.fr: Buck ne s’arrêta pas : il bondit sur l’homme suivant et le tua à son tour.

s.t: A third man hit at him with a stick, but Buck was quicker, and that man fell down.
s.fr: Un troisième homme voulut l’assommer d’un bâton, mais Buck fut plus vif, et l’homme s’écroula.

paras.summary: Buck jumps at the chief of the Yeehats, cuts open his throat, and kills the next man too.

s.t: The Yeehats shouted, and some of them shot arrows at Buck.
s.fr: Les Yeehats hurlaient, et certains décochèrent des flèches sur Buck.

s.t: Buck moved fast, and most of the arrows hit other men.
s.fr: Buck se déplaçait si vite que la plupart des flèches atteignirent d’autres hommes.

s.t: Buck remembered the man in the red sweater, but he was not afraid of men now.
s.fr: Buck se souvint de l’homme au chandail rouge, mais il ne craignait plus les hommes, à présent.

s.t: The law of the club said that a dog must not hurt a man, and Buck did not obey it.
s.fr: La loi du gourdin disait qu’un chien ne doit pas s’en prendre à un homme, et Buck n’en tint aucun compte.

paras.summary: The Yeehats shoot arrows that hit their own men, and Buck is not afraid of men now.

s.t: The Yeehats were afraid, and they ran away into the forest.
s.fr: Pris de peur, les Yeehats s’enfuirent dans la forêt.

s.t: Buck ran after them and killed more of them, and he did not stop until the forest was quiet.
s.fr: Buck les poursuivit, en tua d’autres encore, et ne s’arrêta que lorsque la forêt redevint silencieuse.

s.t: He went back to the camp and looked for Thornton, but he did not see him.
s.fr: Il revint au campement chercher Thornton, mais ne le vit nulle part.

s.t: Buck smelled the ground among the torn things, and he found the trail of his master.
s.fr: Buck flaira le sol parmi les affaires en lambeaux, et il trouva la piste de son maître.

paras.summary: The Yeehats run away, Buck chases and kills more of them, and he goes back to the camp and finds Thornton's trail.

s.t: Thornton's trail went down from the camp to a deep pool, and it did not come back.
s.fr: La piste de Thornton descendait du campement jusqu’à une mare profonde, et ne revenait pas.

s.t: Buck stood at the edge of the pool, and the water was dark.
s.fr: Buck se tenait au bord de la mare, dont l’eau était noire.

s.t: He smelled the ground for a long time, and he found the marks of many feet.
s.fr: Il flaira longtemps le sol et y trouva les empreintes de nombreux pieds.

s.t: At last he put his nose to the water, and he knew what had happened.
s.fr: Enfin, il approcha le museau de l’eau, et il comprit ce qui s’était passé.

s.t: The Yeehats had killed Thornton, and he was in the pool.
s.fr: Les Yeehats avaient tué Thornton, et il gisait au fond de la mare.

paras.summary: Thornton's trail leads to a deep pool and does not come back, and Buck knows that the Yeehats have killed Thornton and he is in the pool.

s.t: Buck lay down at the edge of the water, and he did not eat.
s.fr: Buck se coucha au bord de l’eau et ne mangea rien.

s.t: All that day he lay there and looked at the pool, and no sound came from him.
s.fr: Toute la journée, il resta là, les yeux fixés sur la mare, sans qu’aucun son ne sorte de sa gorge.

s.t: The Yeehats did not come back to the camp, for they were afraid of him.
s.fr: Les Yeehats ne revinrent pas au campement, car il leur faisait peur.

s.t: One arrow had cut his side, and the blood on it was dry, but he did not lick the wound.
s.fr: Une flèche lui avait entaillé le flanc, et le sang y avait séché, mais il ne lécha pas la blessure.

s.t: In the night the moon came up over the trees, and the water was still.
s.fr: Dans la nuit, la lune se leva au-dessus des arbres, et l’eau dormait.

paras.summary: Buck lies by the pool all day and does not eat, the Yeehats stay away, and the moon comes up over the water.

s.t: Buck had loved Thornton more than any man, and now Thornton was dead.
s.fr: Buck avait aimé Thornton plus qu’aucun autre homme, et maintenant Thornton était mort.

s.t: No man was left in the world for Buck, and no man could call him.
s.fr: Il ne restait plus un seul homme au monde pour Buck, et personne ne pourrait plus l’appeler.

s.t: He remembered the farm and the Judge, and he remembered Perrault and Francois.
s.fr: Il se souvint de la ferme et du juge, et il se souvint de Perrault et de François.

s.t: He remembered Dave, and he remembered the club, and he remembered the cold.
s.fr: Il se souvint de Dave, du gourdin et du froid.

s.t: Those days were gone, and Buck was alone.
s.fr: Ces jours-là étaient révolus, et Buck était seul.

paras.summary: Buck knows that no man is left to call him, and he remembers his old masters and the days that are gone.

s.t: Buck had killed men that day, and he knew that no man could hurt him now.
s.fr: Buck avait tué des hommes ce jour-là, et il savait que désormais nul homme ne pourrait lui faire de mal.

s.t: A man with a club or an arrow was only a man, and a man could die.
s.fr: Un homme armé d’un gourdin ou d’une flèche n’était qu’un homme, et un homme, cela pouvait mourir.

s.t: He got up and cried, and it was a long cry, and he cried it to the moon.
s.fr: Il se leva et hurla, d’un long hurlement qu’il adressa à la lune.

s.t: It was the cry of a wolf, and it was the cry that he had heard in the forest.
s.fr: C’était le hurlement d’un loup, celui qu’il avait entendu dans la forêt.

s.t: Far away in the hills another cry answered him, and then a third cry came.
s.fr: Au loin, dans les collines, un autre hurlement lui répondit, puis un troisième s’éleva.

s.t: He lay down by the pool again and listened to the cries in the hills.
s.fr: Il se recoucha près de la mare et écouta les hurlements qui montaient des collines.

paras.summary: Buck knows that no man can hurt him now, cries a long wolf's cry to the moon, and listens to the cries that answer him from the hills.

s.t: The next night the wolves came down from the hills to the camp.
s.fr: La nuit suivante, les loups descendirent des collines jusqu’au campement.

s.t: They came out of the trees one by one, and there were many of them.
s.fr: Ils sortirent d’entre les arbres un à un, et ils étaient nombreux.

s.t: They stood in a ring around Buck, and they did not make a sound.
s.fr: Ils firent cercle autour de Buck, sans faire aucun bruit.

s.t: Buck remembered Curly and the ring of dogs, and he stood still in the moon.
s.fr: Buck se souvint de Curly et du cercle des chiens, et il se tint coi sous la lune.

s.t: He stood with his back to the pool, and no wolf could come at him from behind.
s.fr: Il s’était adossé à la mare, si bien qu’aucun loup ne pouvait le prendre à revers.

paras.summary: The next night many wolves come down from the hills and stand in a ring around Buck, who stands with his back to the pool.

s.t: A big wolf ran at Buck, and Buck cut his neck, and the wolf fell.
s.fr: Un grand loup fonça sur Buck, qui lui ouvrit le cou, et le loup s’abattit.

s.t: Two more wolves came at him together, and Buck fought them as he had fought Spitz.
s.fr: Deux autres loups l’assaillirent à la fois, et Buck se battit contre eux comme il s’était battu contre Spitz.

s.t: He was quick, and he was clever, and he was strong from the forest.
s.fr: Il était vif, il était rusé, et la forêt l’avait rendu fort.

s.t: Three wolves lay dead on the ground, but the ring did not break.
s.fr: Trois loups gisaient morts sur le sol, mais le cercle ne se rompit pas.

s.t: The wolves came again and again, and each time Buck fought them off.
s.fr: Les loups revinrent à la charge encore et encore, et chaque fois Buck les repoussa.

paras.summary: A big wolf attacks Buck, and Buck fights as he fought Spitz, killing three wolves, but the ring does not break.

s.t: He was tired now, and blood ran from his neck and his legs.
s.fr: Il était las à présent, et le sang coulait de son cou et de ses pattes.

s.t: The whole pack came at him together, and Buck stood at the edge of the water and fought them.
s.fr: La meute entière se rua sur lui d’un seul coup, et Buck, au bord de l’eau, lui tint tête.

s.t: At last the wolves stopped and fell back, and they stood in the moon and looked at him.
s.fr: Enfin les loups cessèrent l’attaque et reculèrent, puis restèrent sous la lune à le regarder.

s.t: One wolf came out of the ring, and he was thin and grey.
s.fr: Un loup sortit du cercle, maigre et gris.

s.t: Buck knew him, for this was the wolf who had run with him in the forest.
s.fr: Buck le reconnut : c’était le loup qui avait couru avec lui dans la forêt.

paras.summary: Buck is tired and bleeding when the whole pack attacks, and at last the wolves fall back and the thin grey wolf from the forest comes out.

s.t: The wolf cried softly, and Buck touched noses with him.
s.fr: Le loup gémit doucement, et Buck lui toucha le museau.

s.t: An old wolf came next, and his face was cut in many places.
s.fr: Un vieux loup s’avança ensuite, le museau couturé de cicatrices.

s.t: The old wolf sat down in the moon and lifted his nose to the sky and cried.
s.fr: Le vieux loup s’assit sous la lune, leva le museau vers le ciel et hurla.

s.t: The other wolves sat down and cried too.
s.fr: Les autres loups s’assirent et hurlèrent à leur tour.

paras.summary: Buck touches noses with the thin wolf, and an old wolf sits down and cries, and the other wolves sit and cry too.

s.t: Buck sat down among them, and he lifted his nose to the sky and cried with them.
s.fr: Buck s’assit parmi eux, leva le museau vers le ciel et hurla avec eux.

s.t: It was the cry that he had cried at the pool, and now it came back to him from many voices.
s.fr: C’était le hurlement qu’il avait poussé près de la mare, et à présent il lui revenait, repris par une multitude de voix.

s.t: When the cry was over, the old wolf got up and ran into the forest.
s.fr: Quand le hurlement se tut, le vieux loup se leva et s’élança dans la forêt.

s.t: The pack ran behind him, and the thin wolf ran beside Buck.
s.fr: La meute le suivit, et le loup maigre courait aux côtés de Buck.

s.t: Buck ran with the pack through the trees, and he did not look back at the camp.
s.fr: Buck courut avec la meute à travers les arbres, sans un regard en arrière pour le campement.

paras.summary: Buck cries with the pack, and when the old wolf runs into the forest, Buck runs with the pack beside the thin wolf.

s.t: Many years went by, and the Yeehats saw a change in the wolves of that country.
s.fr: Bien des années passèrent, et les Yeehats remarquèrent un changement chez les loups de la contrée.

s.t: Some of the wolves had brown on their heads and white on their chests, and they were bigger than the other wolves.
s.fr: Certains loups avaient la tête tachée de brun et le poitrail marqué de blanc, et ils étaient plus grands que les autres.

s.t: The Yeehats told each other about a Ghost Dog who ran at the head of the pack.
s.fr: Les Yeehats se racontaient l’histoire d’un Chien Fantôme qui courait en tête de la meute.

s.t: "The Ghost Dog is more clever than any man," they said.
s.fr: « Le Chien Fantôme est plus rusé qu’aucun homme, » disaient-ils.

paras.summary: After many years the Yeehats see that some wolves have brown on their heads and white on their chests, and they say that a Ghost Dog leads the pack.

s.t: "He steals from our camps in the winter, and he kills our dogs."
s.fr: « L’hiver, il vient voler dans nos campements, et il tue nos chiens. »

s.t: "He is not afraid of our knives, and he is not afraid of our arrows."
s.fr: « Il ne craint ni nos couteaux ni nos flèches. »

s.t: Some hunters went into the forest and did not come back.
s.fr: Des chasseurs s’enfoncèrent dans la forêt et n’en revinrent pas.

s.t: Other men found them in the snow, and their throats were cut.
s.fr: D’autres hommes les retrouvèrent dans la neige, la gorge tranchée.

s.t: Around them were the marks of a wolf's feet, and the marks were bigger than the feet of any wolf.
s.fr: Autour d’eux se voyaient des empreintes de loup, plus grandes que celles d’aucun loup.

s.t: "That is the Ghost Dog," the Yeehats said, "and he is killing our men."
s.fr: « C’est le Chien Fantôme, disaient les Yeehats, et il tue nos hommes. »

paras.summary: The Yeehats say the Ghost Dog steals from their camps and kills their dogs, and hunters who go into the forest are found dead with a huge wolf's marks around them.

s.t: The Yeehats did not go near the valley with the pool, for they said that the Ghost Dog lived there.
s.fr: Les Yeehats n’approchaient jamais de la vallée de la mare, car le Chien Fantôme, disaient-ils, y vivait.

s.t: Every summer a wolf came to that valley, and no Yeehat ever saw him there.
s.fr: Chaque été, un loup venait dans cette vallée, et jamais aucun Yeehat ne l’y aperçut.

s.t: He was a big wolf with a thick coat, and he came alone out of the forest.
s.fr: C’était un grand loup à l’épaisse fourrure, qui sortait seul de la forêt.

s.t: He walked down to the pool and stood at the edge of the water.
s.fr: Il descendait jusqu’à la mare et s’arrêtait au bord de l’eau.

s.t: He stayed there for a long time, and he did not move.
s.fr: Il restait là longtemps, sans bouger.

s.t: He lifted his nose to the sky and cried a long cry, and it was a sad cry.
s.fr: Il levait le museau vers le ciel et poussait un long hurlement, un hurlement plein de tristesse.

s.t: When the cry was over, he turned and went back into the forest.
s.fr: Quand le hurlement s’était tu, il faisait demi-tour et regagnait la forêt.

paras.summary: The Yeehats do not go near the valley with the pool, where every summer a big wolf comes alone, stands at the water, and cries a sad cry.

s.t: In the winter the nights were long, and the wolves went out to hunt.
s.fr: L’hiver, les nuits étaient longues, et les loups partaient en chasse.

s.t: The Yeehats saw the big wolf run at the head of the pack in the moon.
s.fr: Les Yeehats voyaient le grand loup courir en tête de la meute, sous la lune.

s.t: He ran faster than any of the other wolves.
s.fr: Il courait plus vite que tous les autres loups.

s.t: He cried the cry of the pack, and the wolves cried it after him.
s.fr: Il lançait le hurlement de la meute, et les loups le reprenaient après lui.

s.t: That wolf was Buck, who had once been a dog on a farm, and now he was the leader of the wolves.
s.fr: Ce loup, c’était Buck, autrefois simple chien de ferme, devenu à présent le chef des loups.

paras.summary: In the winter the Yeehats see the big wolf run at the head of the pack, and he is Buck, the leader of the wolves.
